<!-- eg-1: body_md -->
\label{key_eg}
Consider $\pi : {\mathbb C}^2_{x,\,y}\times({\mathbb C}_{\lambda}\setminus\{0,1\}) \longrightarrow {\mathbb C}_\lambda\setminus\{0,1\}$ and a family of foliations given by 
\[x\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+\lambda y\frac{\partial}{\partial y}.\]
We can extend this family to a family ${\mathbb P}^2\times({\mathbb C}\setminus\{0,1\})\longrightarrow{\mathbb C}\setminus\{0,1\}$. 
Note that the singularity is reduced (see Definition~\ref{semi_reduced}) if and only if $\lambda\not\in{\mathbb Q}^+$.
<!-- end eg-1 -->
<!-- thm-1: body_md -->
Fix a function $P: {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
Then the set ${\mathcal{S}}_P$ consisting of minimal partial du Val resolutions $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)$ (see Definition~\ref{mpdvr}) of log canonical models $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ of general type with Hilbert function $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}}) = P(m)$ is bounded. 
More precisely, there exists a projective morphism $\mu : {\mathcal{Y}} \longrightarrow T$ and a family of foliations ${\mathcal{F}}$ on ${\mathcal{Y}}$ over $T$ (see Definition~\ref{family_fol}) where ${\mathcal{Y}}$ and $T$ are quasi-projective varieties of finite type such that, for any $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, there is a $t\in T$ and an isomorphism $\rho : Y\longrightarrow {\mathcal{Y}}_t$ such that ${\mathscr{G}}(-D) \cong \rho^*({\mathcal{F}}\vert_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t})$.
<!-- end thm-1 -->
<!-- thm-2: body_md -->
Given any family of foliated triples $f : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)\longrightarrow T$ where $T$ is connected 
and $({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)_t\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$ for all $t\in T$ (see Definition~\ref{defn_fol_family} for families of foliated triples), there exists an integer $m_{f}$ depending only on this family $f$ such that  
\[h^0({\mathcal{X}}_t,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}}+\Delta)\vert_{{\mathcal{X}}_t})\] is independent of $t$ for $m\geq m_f$ and divisible by $i(P)$. (See Lemma~\ref{iP}.)
<!-- end thm-2 -->
<!-- thm-3: body_md -->
Let $f : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta) \longrightarrow T$ be a family of foliated triples which is a semi-stable reduction of a family of foliated triples whose general fiber is in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
(See subsection~\ref{ss_reduction}.)
Then the relative $(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\Delta)$-minimal model program exists and stops with a family of foliated triples $({\mathcal{X}}^{\textnormal{m}},{\mathcal{F}}^{\textnormal{m}},\Delta^{\textnormal{m}}) \longrightarrow T$ such that $(K_{{\mathcal{F}}^{\textnormal{m}}}+\Delta^{\textnormal{m}})$ is nef over $T$, $f^{\textnormal{m}} : {\mathcal{X}}^{\textnormal{m}} \longrightarrow T$ is dlt, and the general fiber is in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$.
<!-- end thm-3 -->
<!-- thm-4: body_md -->
Let $T$ be a smooth curve, $T^\circ = T\setminus\{0\}$ where $0\in T$, and $({\mathcal{X}}_i,{\mathcal{F}}_i,\Delta_i) \in{\mathcal{M}}_P^{\textnormal{sm}}(T)$ be two families of stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable foliated triples over $T$ for $i=1$, $2$. 
Then any isomorphism $\varphi^\circ : ({\mathcal{X}}_1,{\mathcal{F}}_1,\Delta_1)_{T^\circ} \longrightarrow ({\mathcal{X}}_2,{\mathcal{F}}_2,\Delta_2)_{T^\circ}$ over $T^\circ$ extends uniquely to an isomorphism $\varphi : ({\mathcal{X}}_1,{\mathcal{F}}_1,\Delta_1) \longrightarrow ({\mathcal{X}}_2,{\mathcal{F}}_2,\Delta_2)$ over $T$.
<!-- end thm-4 -->
<!-- thm-5: body_md -->
Let $T$ be a smooth curve and $({\mathcal{X}}^\circ,{\mathcal{F}}^\circ,\Delta^\circ)\in{\mathcal{M}}_P^{\textnormal{sm}}(T^\circ)$ be a family of stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable foliated triples over $T^\circ$ where $T^\circ = T\setminus\{0\}$ and $0\in T$. 
Suppose the fiber of the family over $t\neq 0$ is in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
Then there exists a smooth curve $C$ and a finite morphism $C \longrightarrow T$ such that, after the base change via $C \longrightarrow T$, the pullback family $({\mathcal{X}}_C^\circ,{\mathcal{F}}_C^\circ,\Delta_C^\circ)$ extends uniquely to a family of stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable foliated triples $({\mathcal{X}}_C,{\mathcal{F}}_C,\Delta_C)$ over $C$.
<!-- end thm-5 -->
<!-- thm-6: body_md -->
Given a family of foliated triples $f : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)\longrightarrow T$. 
($T$ is not necessarily a curve.) 
Assume that there is a dense subset $T'\subset T$ such that $({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)_t\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$ for all $t\in T'$. 
(See Definition~\ref{set_MPdVR} and Definition~\ref{defn_fol_family}.) 
Then there exists an open subset $U\subset T$ such that all fibers of $f$ over $U$ are in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$.
<!-- end thm-6 -->
<!-- acks-1: body_md -->
A large part of the paper was written during the author was at the University of Utah. He would like to thank the University of Utah for wonderful research conditions. The author would also like to thank Christopher D. Hacon for his insightful suggestions and encouragements and Fabio Bernasconi for invaluable discussions.
<!-- end acks-1 -->
<!-- thm-7: body_md -->
\label{va_eff}
Let $X$ be a normal projective surface and $M$ be a ${\mathbb Q}$-divisor on $X$ such that $K_X+\lceil M\rceil$ is Cartier. 
Let $\zeta$ be a 0-dimensional subscheme of $X$ and $\delta_\zeta>0$ be the number defined in \cite[Definition 1.1.2]{langer2001adjoint} associated to $\zeta$. If 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $M^2>\delta_\zeta$ and 
\item $M\cdot C\geq \frac{1}{2}\delta_\zeta$ for every curve $C$ on $X$,  
\end{enumerate}
then $H^0(X,{\mathcal{O}}_X(K_X+\lceil M\rceil)) \longrightarrow {\mathcal{O}}_\zeta(K_X+\lceil M\rceil)$ is surjective.
<!-- end thm-7 -->
<!-- rmk-1: body_md -->
\label{delta}
For the case when $|\zeta| = 2$, we have following remarks. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If the support of $\zeta = \{x_1,x_2\}$ is two distinct points, then $\delta_{\zeta} = \delta_{x_1}+\delta_{x_2}$. (\cite[1.1.3]{langer2001adjoint})
\item $\delta_x \leq 4$ if $x$ is a smooth point or a du Val singularity. (\cite[0.3.2]{langer2001adjoint})
\item If $\zeta$ is supported at only one point $x$, then 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\delta_\zeta \leq 8$ if $x$ is a smooth point or a du Val singularity. (\cite[0.3.2]{langer2001adjoint})
\item $\delta_\zeta \leq 4(\textnormal{edim}_xX-1)$ if $x$ is a rational (non-smooth) singularity where $\textnormal{edim}_xX$ is the embedding dimension of $X$ at $x$. (\cite[0.3.4]{langer2001adjoint})
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end rmk-1 -->
<!-- prop-1: body_md -->
\label{sep}
Let $X$ be a projective scheme over $k$ and ${\mathscr{L}}$ be a line bundle on $X$. 
Then ${\mathscr{L}}$ is very ample if and only if it separates points and tangents.
<!-- end prop-1 -->
<!-- defn-1: body_md -->
\label{defn_fol_sch}
Let $X$ be a scheme. 
A \emph{pre-foliation} ${\mathscr{F}}$ of rank one on $X$ is a rank-one quotient sheaf $\Omega_{{\mathscr{F}}}$ of $\Omega_X^{[**]}$. 
Here $\Omega_X^{[**]}$ is the hull of $\Omega_X$ defined in \cite[Definition 14]{kollar2008hulls}. 
A pre-foliation ${\mathscr{F}}$ is called a \emph{foliation} if it is \emph{pure}, that is, the closure of each associated point of $\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}$ has dimension $\dim X$.
<!-- end defn-1 -->
<!-- lem-1: body_md -->
\label{normal_fol_equiv}
Let $X$ be a normal variety. 
A foliation ${\mathscr{F}}$ of rank one on $X$ is equivalent to a saturated rank one coherent subsheaf $T_{\mathscr{F}}$ of the tangent sheaf $T_X$. 
Here a subsheaf $T_{\mathscr{F}}$ of $T_X$ is called saturated if $T_X/T_{\mathscr{F}}$ is torsion-free.
<!-- end lem-1 -->
<!-- pf-1: body_md -->
Since $X$ is normal, we have $\Omega_X^{[**]} = \Omega_X^{**}$ the double dual of $\Omega_X$. 

Given a foliation ${\mathscr{F}}$ on $X$, we have an exact sequence 
\[\xymatrix{0\ar[r] & K \ar[r] & \Omega_X^{**} \ar[r]^-{\rho_{\mathscr{F}}} & \Omega_{\mathscr{F}} \ar[r] & 0}\]
where $K$ is the kernel of $\rho_{\mathscr{F}}$. 
Dualizing this sequence, we get 
\[\xymatrix{0 \ar[r] & \Omega_{\mathscr{F}}^* \ar[r]^-{\rho_{\mathscr{F}}^*} & T_X \ar[r] & A \ar[r] & 0}\]
where $A$ is the cokernel of $\rho_{\mathscr{F}}^*$. 
Note that $A$ is a subsheaf of $K^*$ and $K^*$ is torsion-free. 
So $A$ is also torsion-free, and thus $\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}^*$ is saturated. 
Therefore, this gives a function $F$ from the set of foliations of rank one on $X$ to the set of saturated rank one coherent subsheaves of the tangent sheaf $T_X$. 

Conversely, given a saturated coherent subsheaf $T_{\mathscr{F}}$ of $T_X$, we have an exact sequence 
\[\xymatrix{0 \ar[r] & T_{\mathscr{F}} \ar[r] & T_X \ar[r]^-\pi & T_X/T_{\mathscr{F}} \ar[r] & 0.}\] 
Dualizing the sequence, we have 
\[\xymatrix{0\ar[r] & (T_X/T_{\mathscr{F}})^* \ar[r]^-{\pi^*} & \Omega_X^{**} \ar[r] & B \ar[r] & 0}\]
where $B$ is the cokernel of $\pi^*$. 
Notice that $B$ is a subsheaf of $T_{\mathscr{F}}^*$ and $T_{\mathscr{F}}^*$ is torsion-free. 
Thus $B$ is also torsion-free and therefore gives a foliation on $X$. 
Hence, this gives a function $G$ from the set of saturated rank one coherent subsheaves of the tangent sheaf $T_X$ to the set of foliations of rank one on $X$. 

Notice that both $G\circ F$ and $F\circ G$ are generically identity functions. 
\begin{claim}
They are indeed identity functions up to isomorphism. 
\end{claim}
\begin{pf}
Notice that we have the following exact sequences: 
\[\xymatrix{0 \ar[r] & K \ar[r] & \Omega_X^{**} \ar[r] \ar@{=}[d] & \Omega_{\mathscr{F}} \ar[r] & 0 \\
0 \ar[r] & A^* \ar[r] & \Omega_X^{**} \ar[r] & G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}})) \ar[r] & 0.}\]
Since $G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}))$ is torsion-free and the map 
\[\xymatrix{K\ar[r] & \Omega_X^{**} \ar[r] & G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}))}\] 
is generically zero, the image is in fact zero in $G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}))$. 
Thus, we have $K\subset A^*$. 
Similarly, we have $A^* \subset K$. 
Therefore, we have $K = A^*$ and hence $\Omega_{\mathscr{F}} \cong G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}))$. 

Similarly, we could show that $T_{\mathscr{F}} = F(G(T_{\mathscr{F}}))$. 
\qed
\end{pf}
<!-- end pf-1 -->
<!-- claim-1: body_md -->
They are indeed identity functions up to isomorphism.
<!-- end claim-1 -->
<!-- pf-2: body_md -->
Notice that we have the following exact sequences: 
\[\xymatrix{0 \ar[r] & K \ar[r] & \Omega_X^{**} \ar[r] \ar@{=}[d] & \Omega_{\mathscr{F}} \ar[r] & 0 \\
0 \ar[r] & A^* \ar[r] & \Omega_X^{**} \ar[r] & G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}})) \ar[r] & 0.}\]
Since $G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}))$ is torsion-free and the map 
\[\xymatrix{K\ar[r] & \Omega_X^{**} \ar[r] & G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}))}\] 
is generically zero, the image is in fact zero in $G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}))$. 
Thus, we have $K\subset A^*$. 
Similarly, we have $A^* \subset K$. 
Therefore, we have $K = A^*$ and hence $\Omega_{\mathscr{F}} \cong G(F(\Omega_{\mathscr{F}}))$. 

Similarly, we could show that $T_{\mathscr{F}} = F(G(T_{\mathscr{F}}))$. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-2 -->
<!-- defn-2: body_md -->
\label{fol_triple}
A \emph{foliated triple} is a triple $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D)$ where $X$ is a scheme, ${\mathscr{F}}$ is a foliation, and $D$ is a reduced divisor. 
When $D=\emptyset$, we call $(X,{\mathscr{F}}) := (X,{\mathscr{F}},\emptyset)$ a \emph{foliated scheme} (resp. \emph{foliated variety}) if $X$ is a scheme (resp. variety).
<!-- end defn-2 -->
<!-- defn-3: body_md -->
A \emph{foliation} ${\mathscr{F}}$ on a normal variety $X$ is a coherent subsheaf ${\mathscr{F}}$ of the tangent sheaf $T_X$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item it is closed under the Lie bracket and 
\item ${\mathscr{F}}$ is saturated, that is, the quotient $T_X/{\mathscr{F}}$ is torsion free.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-3 -->
<!-- rmk-2: body_md -->
By Lemma~\ref{normal_fol_equiv}, this is equivalent to Definition~\ref{defn_fol_sch} when the rank is one.
<!-- end rmk-2 -->
<!-- defn-4: body_md -->
Let ${\mathscr{F}}$ be a foliation on a normal variety $X$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item  Given $f : Y \dashrightarrow X$ be a dominant rational map. 
Let $U$ be an open subset of $X$ such that $f\vert_V : V \longrightarrow U$ is an isomorphism where $V:= f^{-1}(U)$. 
Note that ${\mathscr{F}}\vert_U \subset T_U \cong T_V$. 
By \cite[Exercise II.5.15]{hartshorne1977algebraic}, there is a coherent subsheaf ${\mathscr{G}}$ of $T_Y$ such that ${\mathscr{G}}\vert_V = {\mathscr{F}}\vert_U \subset T_V $. 
Then the \emph{pullback foliation} $f^*{\mathscr{F}}$ is defined to be the saturation of ${\mathscr{G}}$. 
Note that ${\mathscr{G}}$ is closed under the Lie bracket and, by \cite[Lemma 1.8]{hacon2021birational}, this definition is well-defined. 
\item Given $g : X \dashrightarrow Z$ be a birational map, then we define the \emph{pushforward foliation} $g_*{\mathscr{F}}$ as $(g^{-1})^*{\mathscr{F}}$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-4 -->
<!-- defn-5: body_md -->
Let ${\mathscr{F}}$ be a foliation on a normal variety $X$. 
Given a subvariety $W$ of $X$. 
Let $U = X\setminus\left(\textnormal{Sing}(X)\cup\textnormal{Sing}({\mathscr{F}})\cup\textnormal{Sing}(W)\right)$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $W$ is \emph{tangent} to ${\mathscr{F}}$ if $T_W\vert_U\longrightarrow T_X\vert_U$ factors through ${\mathscr{F}}\vert_U$. 
Otherwise we say $W$ is \emph{transverse} to ${\mathscr{F}}$. 
\item $W$ is \emph{invariant} if ${\mathscr{F}}\vert_U\longrightarrow T_X\vert_U$ factors through $T_W\vert_U$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-5 -->
<!-- defn-6: body_md -->
We define Kodaira dimension of ${\mathscr{F}}$ as 
\[\kappa({\mathscr{F}}) = \max\{\dim\phi_{|mK_{\mathscr{F}}|}(X)\vert\,m\in{\mathbb N}_{>0} \mbox{ and } h^0(X,mK_{\mathscr{F}})>0\}\] 
where by convention $\kappa({\mathscr{F}})=-\infty$ if the set above is empty, that is, $h^0(X,mK_{\mathscr{F}})=0$ for all $m\in{\mathbb N}_{>0}$. 
We say that ${\mathscr{F}}$ is \emph{of general type} if $\kappa(K_{\mathscr{F}}) = \dim X$.
<!-- end defn-6 -->
<!-- defn-7: body_md -->
Let $({\mathscr{F}},\Delta)$ be a foliated pair on a normal variety $X$ and $f : Y\longrightarrow X$ be a proper birational morphism. 
For any divisor $E$ on $Y$, we define the \emph{discrepancy} of $({\mathscr{F}},\Delta)$ along $E$ to be $a(E,{\mathscr{F}},\Delta) = \textnormal{ord}_E(K_{f^*{\mathscr{F}}}-f^*(K_{\mathscr{F}}+\Delta))$. 

We say $(X,{\mathscr{F}},\Delta)$ is \emph{terminal} (resp. \emph{canonical}) if $a(E,{\mathscr{F}},\Delta)> 0$ (resp. $\geq 0$) for every exceptional divisor $E$ over $X$ and 
$(X,{\mathscr{F}},\Delta)$ is \emph{log terminal} (resp. \emph{log canonical}) if $a(E,{\mathscr{F}},\Delta)> -\varepsilon(E)$ (resp. $\geq -\varepsilon(E)$) for every divisor $E$ over $X$ where $\varepsilon(E)$ is defined to be $0$ if $E$ is $f^*{\mathscr{F}}$-invariant, and $1$ otherwise.
<!-- end defn-7 -->
<!-- defn-8: body_md -->
\label{index}
Let $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be a foliated normal variety. 
We have the following definitions for indices.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The index $i(X)$ of $X$ is the smallest positive integer $m$ such that $mD$ is Cartier for every Weil divisor $D$ on $X$. 
(We set $i(X)=\infty$ if there is no such $m$.)
\item The index $i(K_X)$ of $K_X$ is the smallest positive integer $m$ such that $mK_X$ is Cartier. 
(We set $i(K_X)=\infty$ if $K_X$ is not ${\mathbb Q}$-Cartier.)
\item The index $i({\mathscr{F}})$ of a foliation ${\mathscr{F}}$ on $X$ is the smallest positive integer $m$ such that $mK_{\mathscr{F}}$ is Cartier. 
(We set $i({\mathscr{F}})=\infty$ if $K_{\mathscr{F}}$ is not ${\mathbb Q}$-Cartier.)
\item The ${\mathbb Q}$-index $i_{\mathbb Q}({\mathscr{F}})$ of a foliation ${\mathscr{F}}$ on $X$ is the smallest positive integer $m$ such that $mK_{\mathscr{F}}$ is Cartier for all ${\mathbb Q}$-Gorenstein points of the foliation. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-8 -->
<!-- defn-9: body_md -->
\label{semi_reduced}
If one of the eigenvalues is non-zero, say $\lambda_2$, then we define the eigenvalue of the foliation ${\mathscr{F}}$ at $p$ to be 
\[\lambda := \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}.\] 
For $\lambda\neq 0$, this definition is unique up to reciprocal $\lambda \sim \frac{1}{\lambda}$. 

If $\lambda = 0$, then $p$ is called a \emph{saddle-node}; otherwise, we say $p$ is \emph{non-degenerate}. 
If $\lambda\not\in{\mathbb Q}^+$, then $p$ is called a \emph{reduced} singularity of ${\mathscr{F}}$.
<!-- end defn-9 -->
<!-- thm-8: body_md -->
Given any foliated surface $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ with $X$ smooth. 
Then there is a sequence of blowups $\pi : (Y,{\mathscr{G}}) \longrightarrow (X,{\mathscr{F}})$ such that $(Y,{\mathscr{G}})$ has only reduced singularities.
<!-- end thm-8 -->
<!-- pf-3: body_md -->
See \cite{seidenberg1968reduction}, \cite[Appendix]{mattei1980holonomie}, or \cite[Theorem 1.1]{brunella2015birational}. \qed
<!-- end pf-3 -->
<!-- defn-10: body_md -->
Let $p$ be a singular point of ${\mathscr{F}}$. 
A \emph{separatrix} of ${\mathscr{F}}$ at $p$ is a holomorphic (possibly singular) irreducible ${\mathscr{F}}$-invariant curve $C$ on a \emph{neighborhood} of $p$ which passes through $p$.
<!-- end defn-10 -->
<!-- thm-9: body_md -->
\label{separatrix}
Let ${\mathscr{F}}$ be a foliation on a surface $X$ and $C\subset X$ be a connected, compact ${\mathscr{F}}$-invariant curve such that the followings hold.
\begin{enumerate}
\item All the singularities of ${\mathscr{F}}$ on $C$ are reduced and on the non-singular locus of $X$. 
\item The intersection matrix of $C$ is negative definite, and the dual graph is a tree.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists at least one point $p\in C\cap\textnormal{Sing}({\mathscr{F}})$ and a separatrix through $p$ not contained in $C$.
<!-- end thm-9 -->
<!-- pf-4: body_md -->
See \cite{camacho1988quadratic}, \cite{sebastiani1997existence}, or \cite[Theorem 3.4]{brunella2015birational}. \qed
<!-- end pf-4 -->
<!-- defn-11: body_md -->
Let $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be a foliated normal surface and $p\in\textnormal{Sing}({\mathscr{F}})\setminus\textnormal{Sing}(X)$. 
Let $v$ be the vector field generating ${\mathscr{F}}$ around $p$ and $C$ be a \emph{non-invariant} curve through $p$. 
Let $f$ be the local defining function of $C$ at $p$.  
We define the \emph{tangency order} of ${\mathscr{F}}$ along $C$ at $p$ to be 
\[\textnormal{tang}({\mathscr{F}},C,p) := \dim_{\mathbb C}\frac{{\mathcal{O}}_{X,p}}{\langle f,v(f)\rangle}.\]
Note that $\textnormal{tang}({\mathscr{F}},C,p)\geq 0$ and is independent of the choices of $v$ and $f$. 
Moreover, if ${\mathscr{F}}$ is transverse to $C$ at $p$, then $\textnormal{tang}({\mathscr{F}},C,p) = 0$. 
Therefore, if $C$ is compact, then we can define 
\[\textnormal{tang}({\mathscr{F}},C) := \sum_{p\in C}\textnormal{tang}({\mathscr{F}},C,p). \]
<!-- end defn-11 -->
<!-- thm-10: body_md -->
\label{adjunct_non_inv}
Let ${\mathscr{F}}$ be a foliation on a smooth projective surface $X$. 
Let $C$ be a non-invariant irreducible curve on $X$ and $C^\nu$ be the normalization of $C$.  
Then there is an effective divisor $\Delta$ on $C^\nu$ such that $(K_{\mathscr{F}}+C)\vert_{C^\nu} = \Delta$ with $\textnormal{deg}\,\Delta = \textnormal{tang}({\mathscr{F}},C)$.
<!-- end thm-10 -->
<!-- cor-1: body_md -->
Let $C$ be a non-invariant curve on a foliated surface $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$. If $C$ is contained in the smooth locus of $X$, then we have $(K_{\mathscr{F}} + C)\cdot C \geq 0$.
<!-- end cor-1 -->
<!-- defn-12: body_md -->
Let $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be a foliated surface and $p\in\textnormal{Sing}({\mathscr{F}})\setminus\textnormal{Sing}(X)$. 
Let $\omega$ be a $1$-form generating ${\mathscr{F}}$ around $p$. 
If $C$ is an invariant curve and $f$ is the local defining function at $p$, then we can write \[g\omega = h\textnormal{d}f+f\eta\] where $g$ and $h$ are holomorphic functions, $\eta$ is a holomorphic $1$-form, and $h, f$ are relatively prime functions. 

We define the index $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},C,p)$ to be the vanishing order of $\frac{h}{g}\vert_C$ at $p$. 
Also we define Camacho-Sad index $\textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},C,p)$ to be the residue of $\frac{-1}{h}\eta\vert_C$ at $p$.  
These two definitions are independent of the choices of $f$, $g$, $h$, $\omega$, $\eta$. 
(For a reference, see \cite[page 15 in Chapter 2 and page 27 in Chapter 3]{brunella2015birational}.)
<!-- end defn-12 -->
<!-- thm-11: body_md -->
\label{adjunct_inv}
Let ${\mathscr{F}}$ be a foliation on a smooth projective surface $X$. 
Let $C$ be an invariant irreducible curve on $X$ and $C^\nu$ be its normalization. 
Then there is an effective divisor $\Delta$ on $C^\nu$ such that $K_{\mathscr{F}}\vert_{C^\nu} = K_{C^\nu}+\Delta$ with $\deg\Delta = \textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},C) + \deg\textnormal{Diff}_C(0)$ where $\textnormal{Diff}_C(0)$ is the different with $(K_X+C)\vert_{C^\nu} = K_{C^\nu}+\textnormal{Diff}_C(0)$. 
In particular, we have $K_{\mathscr{F}}\cdot C = \textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},C) + 2p_a(C)-2$ where $p_a(C)$ is the arithmetic genus of $C$.
<!-- end thm-11 -->
<!-- thm-12: body_md -->
\label{thm_CS_formula}
Let ${\mathscr{F}}$ be a foliation on a smooth projective surface $X$, and $C$ be an invariant curve on $X$. 
Then we have $C^2 = \textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},C)$.
<!-- end thm-12 -->
<!-- lem-2: body_md -->
\label{lem_ZCS}
Given a foliated normal surface $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$. 
Let $p\in\textnormal{Sing}({\mathscr{F}})\setminus\textnormal{Sing}(X)$ and $\omega$ be a $1$-form generating ${\mathscr{F}}$ around $p$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item Suppose $p$ is reduced and non-degenerate singularity. 
Then we may assume that $\omega = \lambda y(1+o(1))\textnormal{d}x-x(1+o(1))\textnormal{d}y$ around $p$. 
Hence, 
\begin{align*}
& \textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},x=0,p) = \frac{1}{\lambda}, \textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},y=0,p) = \lambda \mbox{, and } \\
& \textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},x=0,p)=1=\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},y=0,p).
\end{align*}
\item Suppose $p$ is a saddle-node. 
Then we may assume that 
\[\omega = y^{k+1}\textnormal{d}x-(x(1+\nu y^k)+yo(k))\textnormal{d}y\] 
around $p$. Hence,  $\textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},y=0,p) = 0$ and $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},y=0,p) = 1$.
Suppose there exists a weak separatrix, then $\textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},x=0,p) = \nu \mbox{ and } \textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},x=0,p) = k+1$.

\item Suppose ${\mathscr{F}}$ has a positive rational eigenvalue $\lambda = \frac{m}{n}\in{\mathbb Q}^+$ in the reduced form at $p$. 
Then we may assume $\omega = \lambda y(1+o(1))\textnormal{d}x-x(1+o(1))\textnormal{d}y$ around $p$. 
Hence, 
\begin{align*}
& \textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},x=0,p) = \frac{1}{\lambda},\,\textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},y=0,p) = \lambda,\,\mbox{and } \\
& \textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},x=0,p)=1=\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},y=0,p).
\end{align*}
Moreover, for the invariant curve $C$ through $p=(0,0)$ which is locally defined by $ax^m(1+o(1))-y^n(1+o(1))=0$, we have 
\begin{align*}
& \textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},C,p) = mn \mbox{ and } \\
& \textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},C,p) = 1-(m-1)(n-1). 
\end{align*}

\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-2 -->
<!-- pf-5: body_md -->
We will only show the case $(3)$. 
For the first two cases, the computations are similar. 
(See also \cite[page 30-31 in Chapter 3]{brunella2015birational}.) 

For the case $f=x$, note that $1\cdot\omega = (\lambda y(1+o(1)))\textnormal{d}x+x(-(1+o(1))\textnormal{d}y)$. 
Then we take $g=1$, $h=\lambda y(1+o(1))$, and $\eta = -(1+o(1))\textnormal{d}y$. 
Thus we have 
\[\textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},x=0,p) = \textnormal{res}_{p}\frac{-1}{h}\eta\vert_{f=0} 
= \textnormal{res}_{p}\frac{1}{\lambda y(1+o(1))}(1+o(1))\textnormal{d}y\vert_{x=0} = \frac{1}{\lambda}\]
and 
\begin{align*}
Z({\mathscr{F}},x=0,p) &= \textnormal{vanishing order of } \frac{h}{g}\vert_{f=0} \\
&= \textnormal{vanishing order of } \frac{\lambda y(1+o(1))}{1}\vert_{x=0} \\
&= 1.
\end{align*}

For the case $f=y$, it is similar. 

For the case $C = (ax^m(1+o(1))-y^n(1+o(1))=0)$, we may assume, for simplicity, that $C = (f=ax^m-y^n=0)$ and $\omega = my\textnormal{d}x-nx\textnormal{d}y$. 
Note that 
\begin{align*}
ax^{m-1}\omega &= amx^{m-1}y\textnormal{d}x - anx^m\textnormal{d}y \\
&= amx^{m-1}y\textnormal{d}x - ny^n\textnormal{d}y - nf\textnormal{d}y \\
&= y\textnormal{d}f-nf\textnormal{d}y.
\end{align*}
So we take $g = ax^{m-1}$, $h=y$, and $\eta = -n\textnormal{d}y$. 
Thus, \[\textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},C,p) = \textnormal{res}_{p}\frac{-1}{h}\eta\vert_{f=0} 
= \textnormal{res}_{p}\,\frac{1}{y}n\textnormal{d}y\vert_{f=0} = mn\]
and 
\begin{align*}
\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},C,p) &= \textnormal{vanishing order of } \frac{h}{g}\vert_{f=0} \\
&= \textnormal{vanishing order of } \frac{y}{ax^{m-1}}\vert_{f=0} \\
&= 1-(n-1)(m-1). 
\end{align*}
\qed
<!-- end pf-5 -->
<!-- defn-13: body_md -->
Let $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be a foliated surface with $X$ smooth and let $\pi: Y\longrightarrow X$ be a birational morphism. 
Denote ${\mathscr{G}}$ be the pullback foliation of ${\mathscr{F}}$ via $\pi$. 
If $E$ is a prime exceptional divisor of $\pi$, then we define the \emph{adjoint discrepancy} of ${\mathscr{F}}$ along $E$ to be the function 
\[a({\mathscr{F}},E) : [0,\infty)\longrightarrow {\mathbb R}\] 
which sends $t$ to $\mbox{\rm ord}_E\big((1-t)(K_{\mathscr{G}}-\pi^*K_{\mathscr{F}}) + t(K_Y-\pi^*K_X)\big)$.
<!-- end defn-13 -->
<!-- defn-14: body_md -->
A point $x$ on a foliated surface $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ with $X$ smooth is called $\varepsilon$-canonical if the adjoint discrepancy of ${\mathscr{F}}$ along any divisor $E$ over $x$ satisfies $a({\mathscr{F}},E)(t)\geq 0$ for every $t\geq \varepsilon$.
<!-- end defn-14 -->
<!-- lem-3: body_md -->
Let $({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}})$ be a smooth family over an algebraic variety $T$ such that all fibers are smooth projective surfaces. 
If $0<\varepsilon<\frac{1}{4}$, then the subset of $T$ corresponding to foliations with isolated and $\varepsilon$-canonical singularities is a Zariski open subset of $T$.
<!-- end lem-3 -->
<!-- prop-2: body_md -->
\label{ve_Sei}
Given a smooth family $({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}})$ over $T$ such that all fibers are smooth projective surfaces and a real number $\varepsilon$ with $0<\varepsilon < \frac{1}{4}$. 
Then there exists a non-empty Zariski open subset $U\subset T$ and a family $({\mathcal{Y}},{\mathcal{G}})$ over $U$ obtained from ${\mathcal{F}}\vert_U$ by a finite composition of blowups over (multi)-sections such that, for all $t\in U$, the foliation ${\mathcal{G}}_t$ has at worst $\varepsilon$-canonical singularities. 
In particular, ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$ is smooth and ${\mathcal{G}}_t$ has at worst log canonical singularities for all $t\in U$.
<!-- end prop-2 -->
<!-- defn-15: body_md -->
Let $X \longrightarrow S$ be a scheme of finite type over a noetherian base scheme $S$ and ${\mathcal{E}}$ be a coherent sheaf on $X$. 
We consider the functor 
\[{\mathcal{Q}} uot_{{\mathcal{E}}/X/S} : (\textnormal{Sch}/S)^{\textnormal{op}} \longrightarrow (\textnormal{Sets})\]
sending $T\longrightarrow S$ to the set 
\[{\mathcal{Q}} uot_{{\mathcal{E}}/X/S}(T) = \left\{({\mathcal{F}},q)\Big\vert 
\begin{array}{l}
{\mathcal{F}}\in\textnormal{Coh}(X_T), \mbox{{\rm Supp}}{{\mathcal{F}}} \textnormal{ is proper over } T \\
{\mathcal{F}} \textnormal{ is flat over } T, q:{\mathcal{E}}_T\longrightarrow {\mathcal{F}} \textnormal{ is surjective.}
\end{array}\right\}\Big/\sim
\]
where $X_T = X\times_ST$, ${\mathcal{E}}_T = \textnormal{pr}_X^*{\mathcal{E}}$ under the projection $\textnormal{pr}_X : X_T \longrightarrow X$, and $({\mathcal{F}} , q ) \sim ( {\mathcal{F}}', q')$ if $\ker q = \ker q'$.
<!-- end defn-15 -->
<!-- defn-16: body_md -->
\label{Hilbert_poly}
Let $X \longrightarrow S$ be a scheme of a finite type over a noetherian base scheme $S$ and ${\mathcal{A}}$ be a relatively ample line bundle. 
For any coherent sheaf ${\mathcal{F}}$ on $X$ flat over $S$, we define the Hilbert polynomial $\Phi_{\mathcal{F}}$ with respect to ${\mathcal{A}}$ as \[\Phi_{\mathcal{F}}(m) = \chi({\mathcal{F}}_s(m)) = \sum_{i=0}^{\dim X}(-1)^ih^i(X_s, {\mathcal{F}}_s\otimes{\mathcal{A}}_s^{\otimes m})\]
for any fixed $s\in S$. 
Note that this definition is independent of the choice of $s\in S$.
<!-- end defn-16 -->
<!-- prop-3: body_md -->
Fix any relatively ample line bundle ${\mathcal{A}}$ on $X$. 
There is a natural stratification: 
\[{\mathcal{Q}} uot_{{\mathcal{E}}/X/S} = \coprod_{\Phi\in{\mathbb Q}[\lambda]}{\mathcal{Q}} uot_{{\mathcal{E}}/X/S}^{\Phi,{\mathcal{A}}}\]
where ${\mathcal{Q}} uot_{{\mathcal{E}}/X/S}^{\Phi,{\mathcal{A}}}(T) = \{({\mathcal{F}},q)\in{\mathcal{Q}} uot_{{\mathcal{E}}/X/S}(T)\,\vert\, \Phi_{\mathcal{F}} = \Phi\}$.
<!-- end prop-3 -->
<!-- thm-13: body_md -->
\label{quot_exist}
The functor ${\mathcal{Q}} uot_{{\mathcal{E}}/X/S}^{\Phi,{\mathcal{A}}}$ is representable by a projective scheme $\textnormal{Quot}_{{\mathcal{E}}/X/S}^{\Phi,{\mathcal{A}}}$ over $S$.
<!-- end thm-13 -->
<!-- defn-17: body_md -->
\label{defn_gcm}
A foliated normal surface $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ is called a \emph{log canonical model} if the following conditions hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\mathscr{F}}$ has \emph{mild} log canonical foliation singularities, that is, ${\mathscr{F}}$ is a foliation with only log canonical foliation singularities such that all points at which ${\mathscr{F}}$ is \emph{not} canonical are either smooth points of $X$ or cyclic quotient singularities of $X$.
\item $K_{\mathscr{F}}$ is nef. 
\item $K_{\mathscr{F}}\cdot C = 0$ implies $C^2\geq 0$ for any irreducible curve $C$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-17 -->
<!-- eg-2: body_md -->
We consider the germ of the normal surface $(x^{n+2}+y^{n+1}+xz^n=0)$ at the origin for $n\geq 2$. 
It is not a rational singularity but the foliation given by 
\[\partial = n(n+1)x\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+n(n+2)y\frac{\partial}{\partial y}+(n+1)^2z\frac{\partial}{\partial z}\]
is log canonical.
<!-- end eg-2 -->
<!-- defn-18: body_md -->
We say a foliated normal surface $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ is a \emph{canonical model} if it is a log canonical model with only canonical foliation singularities.
<!-- end defn-18 -->
<!-- lem-4: body_md -->
\label{ample}
Let $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be a log canonical model. 
If the foliation ${\mathscr{F}}$ is of general type, then $K_{{\mathscr{F}}}$ is numerically ample, that is $K_{{\mathscr{F}}}^2>0$ and $K_{{\mathscr{F}}}\cdot C>0$ for any irreducible curve $C$ on $X$.
<!-- end lem-4 -->
<!-- pf-6: body_md -->
The proof follows closely from the proof of \cite[Lemma 1.11]{hacon2021birational}. \qed
<!-- end pf-6 -->
<!-- defn-19: body_md -->
\label{-2curve}
Given a foliated surface $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ with $X$ smooth. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $E = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_i$ is called a string if 
\begin{enumerate}
\item each $E_i$ is a smooth rational curve and 
\item $E_i\cdot E_j = 1$ if $|i-j|=1$ and $0$ if $|i-j|\geq 2$. 
\end{enumerate}
\item If, moreover, $E_i^2\leq -2$ for all $i$, then we call $E$ a Hirzebruch-Jung string. 
\item A curve $C\subset X$ is called ${\mathscr{F}}$-exceptional if 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $C$ is a $(-1)$-curve and 
\item the contraction of $C$ introduces $(X',{\mathscr{F}}')$ with only \emph{reduced} singularities. 
\end{enumerate}

\item An ${\mathscr{F}}$-invariant curve $C$ is called a $(-1)$-${\mathscr{F}}$-curve (resp. $(-2)$-${\mathscr{F}}$-curve) if 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $C$ is a smooth rational curve and 
\item $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},C)=1$ (resp. $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},C)=2$). 
\end{enumerate}

\item We say $C=\bigcup_{i=1}^sC_i$ is an ${\mathscr{F}}$-chain if 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $C$ is a Hirzebruch-Jung string, 
\item each $C_i$ is ${\mathscr{F}}$-invariant, 
\item $\textnormal{Sing}{{\mathscr{F}}}\cap C$ are all reduced and non-degenerate, and 
\item $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}}, C_1) = 1$ and $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},C_i) = 2$ for all $i\geq 2$. 
\end{enumerate}

\item If an ${\mathscr{F}}$-invariant curve $E$ is not contained in an ${\mathscr{F}}$-chain $C$ but meets the chain, 
then we call $E$ the tail of the chain $C$. 

\item $C$ is called a bad tail if 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $C$ is a smooth rational curve with $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},C) = 3$ and $C^2\leq -2$ and 
\item $C$ intersects two $(-1)$-${\mathscr{F}}$-curves whose self-intersections are both $-2$. 
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-19 -->
<!-- thm-14: body_md -->
\label{struct_can}
Given any canonical model $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$. 
Let $\pi: Y \longrightarrow X$ be the minimal resolution at points at which ${\mathscr{F}}$ is singular. 
Let ${\mathscr{G}}$ be the pullback foliation on $Y$. 
Then all connected components of exceptional divisors of $\pi$ are one of the following types:
\begin{enumerate}
\item ($A_n$ type) A string of smooth rational curves. 
More precisely, it consists of either a ${\mathscr{G}}$-chain, two $(-1)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves of self-intersections $-2$ joined by a bad tail, or a chain of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves.
\item ($D_n$ type) Two $(-1)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves of self-intersections $-2$ joined by a bad tail which itself connects to a chain of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves. 
\item (e.g.l.) Elliptic Gorenstein leaves. That is, either a cycle of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves or a rational curve with only one node.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-14 -->
<!-- lem-5: body_md -->
\label{pos_rat}
Let $(X,{\mathscr{F}},p)$ be a germ of a foliated surface with $p\in X$ a smooth point. 
Suppose ${\mathscr{F}}$ at $p$ has the positive rational eigenvalue. 
Then there is a sequence of blowups $\pi : (Y,{\mathscr{G}}) \longrightarrow (X,{\mathscr{F}},p)$ with ${\mathscr{G}}$ having only reduced singularities on the exceptional divisor $E$. 
Moreover we have the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The support of the exceptional divisor $\bigcup_{i=1}^sE_i$ is a string, 
\item All $E_i$'s except for one $j\in\{1,\ldots,s\}$ are invariant; while this $E_j$ is non-invariant with $\textnormal{tang}({\mathscr{G}},E_j)=0$. 
\item The string $\bigcup_{i=1}^{j-1}E_i$ (resp. $\bigcup_{i=j+1}^{s}E_i$) is a ${\mathscr{G}}$-chain with the first curve $E_{j-1}$ (resp. $E_{j+1}$). 
\item $\pi^*K_{\mathscr{F}} = K_{\mathscr{G}} + E_j$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-5 -->
<!-- pf-7: body_md -->
Since the eigenvalue is defined up to reciprocal, we may assume that the eigenvalue is $\frac{m}{n}\in{\mathbb Q}^+$ with $\textnormal{gcd}(m,n)=1$ and $m\geq n$. 
We proceed by induction on the pair $(m,n)\in{\mathbb N}\times{\mathbb N}$ (by lexicographic ordering). 
\begin{enumerate}
\item We may assume that $p=(0,0)$ and that ${\mathscr{F}}$ is generated by 
\[v = nx\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+my\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\] 
around $p$. 
Let $\varphi : (Y,{\mathscr{G}})\longrightarrow (X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be the blowup at $p$ and $E_0$ be the exceptional divisor. 
Notice that there are two singularities on the exceptional curve locally generated by 
\[v_1 = nx'\frac{\partial}{\partial x'}+(m-n)y'\frac{\partial}{\partial y'}\]
and 
\[v_2 = (n-m)x'\frac{\partial}{\partial x'}+my'\frac{\partial}{\partial y'}.\]

\item For the base case $(m,n) = (1,1)$, by the computation above, the exceptional curve $E_0$ has no foliation singularity and is not invariant with $\textnormal{tang}({\mathscr{G}},E_0) = 0$. 
Moreover, we have $\pi^*K_{\mathscr{F}} = K_{\mathscr{G}}+E_0$. 
Thus, we complete the proof of the base case. 

\item Assume $(m,n)\neq (1,1)$ and all pairs (strictly) less than $(m,n)$ have the desired properties. 
Then $E_0$ is invariant and $\pi^*K_{\mathscr{F}} = K_{\mathscr{G}}$. 
Notice that $v_1$ still has positive rational eigenvalue with corresponding pair $(m-n,n)$ or $(n,m-n)$ while $v_2$ is reduced. 

By induction hypothesis, $v_1$ has a sequence of blowups $\psi : (Z,{\mathscr{H}}) \longrightarrow (Y,{\mathscr{G}})$ with exceptional divisor $E = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_i$. 
Since the proper transform $\widetilde{E}_0$ of $E_0$ on $Z$ meets $E$, $\widetilde{E}_0$ can only meet $E$ as a tail of an ${\mathscr{H}}$-chain. 
Note that $\widetilde{E}_0^2\leq E_0^2-1=-2$. 
Thus, $\widetilde{E}_0$ is a member of that ${\mathscr{H}}$-chain. 
Also $\psi^*\pi^*K_{\mathscr{F}} = \psi^*K_{\mathscr{G}} = K_{\mathscr{H}}+E_i$ for some $i$.
\qed
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end pf-7 -->
<!-- rmk-3: body_md -->
\label{mlc}
By \cite[Fact I.2.4 and its remarks]{mcquillan2008canonical}, a mild log canonical foliation singularity $p$ (see Definition~\ref{defn_gcm}) is formally locally of the form $\partial = x\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+\lambda y\frac{\partial}{\partial y}$ quotient by ${\mathbb Z}/n$ for some $n\in{\mathbb Z}$ and $\lambda\in{\mathbb Q}^+$. 
Also $K_{\mathscr{F}}$ is Cartier around $p$. 
Let $\pi : Y\longrightarrow X$ be the \emph{minimal} resolution of $X$ at $p$ and ${\mathscr{G}}$ be the pullback foliation on $Y$. 
Then, after some computations, we have the following:
\begin{enumerate}
\item The support of the exceptional divisor $E = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_i$ is a string. 
\item For general $\lambda\in{\mathbb Q}^+$, all $E_i$'s are $(-2)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves, exactly one foliation singularity $q$ on $E$ is not reduced, and ${\mathscr{G}}$ has the positive rational eigenvalue at $q$.  
\item Fix the action of ${\mathbb Z}/n$ on $\partial$, for any $j\in\{1,\ldots,s\}$, there is a $\lambda\in{\mathbb Q}^+$ such that $E_j$ is ${\mathscr{G}}$-non-invariant with $\textnormal{tang}({\mathscr{G}},E_j)=0$, the string $\bigcup_{i=1}^{j-1}E_i$ (resp. $\bigcup_{i=j+1}^{s}E_i$) is a ${\mathscr{G}}$-chain with the first curve $E_{j-1}$ (resp. $E_{j+1}$), and $\pi^*K_{\mathscr{F}} = K_{\mathscr{G}} + E_j$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end rmk-3 -->
<!-- eg-3: body_md -->
Consider the foliation of the form $\partial = x\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+\lambda y\frac{\partial}{\partial y}$ on the germ $({\mathbb C}^2/\mu_7,0)$ of the type $\frac{1}{7}(1,4)$. 
Let $Y\longrightarrow X$ be the minimal resolution of singularities. 
Then we have two irreducible exceptional divisors $E_1$ and $E_2$, and we need three copies of ${\mathbb C}^2$ to cover $Y$. 
More explicitly, $Y = {\mathbb C}^2_{\xi_0,\eta_0}\cup{\mathbb C}^2_{\xi_1,\eta_1}\cup{\mathbb C}^2_{\xi_2,\eta_2} = {\mathbb A}^2_0\cup{\mathbb A}^2_1\cup{\mathbb A}^2_2$ 
where \[\begin{array}{lll}
\xi_0=x^{-4}y, & \xi_1 = x^{-1}y^2, & \xi_2 = y^7 \\
\eta_0 = x^7, & \eta_1 = x^4y^{-1}, & \eta_2 = xy^{-2}
\end{array}\]
Thus, on ${\mathbb C}^2_{\xi_0,\eta_0}$, we have 
\[\partial_0 = (\lambda-4)\xi_0\frac{\partial}{\partial \xi_0}+7\eta_0\frac{\partial}{\partial \eta_0}.\]
On ${\mathbb C}^2_{\xi_1,\eta_1}$, we have 
\[\partial_1 = (2\lambda-1)\xi_1\frac{\partial}{\partial \xi_1}+(4-\lambda)\eta_1\frac{\partial}{\partial \eta_1}.\]
And on ${\mathbb C}^2_{\xi_2,\eta_2}$, we have 
\[\partial_2 = 7\lambda\xi_2\frac{\partial}{\partial \xi_2}+(1-2\lambda)\eta_2\frac{\partial}{\partial \eta_2}.\]
Assume that $E_1$ is on ${\mathbb A}^2_0\cup{\mathbb A}^2_1$ and thus defined by $\eta_0=0$ on ${\mathbb A}^2_0$ and by $\xi_1=0$ on ${\mathbb A}^2_1$. 
So $E_2$ is on ${\mathbb A}^2_1\cup{\mathbb A}^2_2$ and defined by $\eta_1=0$ on ${\mathbb A}^2_1$ and by $\xi_2=0$ on ${\mathbb A}^2_2$. 

Therefore, if $\lambda = 4$, then $E_1$ is non-invariant. 
Also if $\lambda = \frac{1}{2}$, then $E_2$ is non-invariant. 
For other $\lambda\in{\mathbb Q}^+$, the exceptional curves $E_1$ and $E_2$ are both invariant, and precisely one of three foliation singularities has positive rational eigenvalue for the foliation.
<!-- end eg-3 -->
<!-- thm-15: body_md -->
\label{description_GenCanModel}
Let $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be a log canonical model. 
Let $\pi: Y \longrightarrow X$ be the minimal resolution at points at which ${\mathscr{F}}$ is singular. 
Let ${\mathscr{G}}$ be the pullback foliation on $Y$. 
Write $K_{\mathscr{G}}+D = \pi^*K_{\mathscr{F}}+E$ where $D$ and $E$ are effective and have no common components. 
Then ${\mathscr{G}}$ has at mild log canonical singularities, $D$ is reduced, the support of $E$ is the union of ${\mathscr{G}}$-chains which are disjoint from $D$, and all irreducible components of $D$ are pairwise disjoint with tangency order zero. 
Moreover, the connected components of $\pi$-exceptional divisors belong to one of the following types: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item ($A_n$ type) A chain of rational invariant curves consisting of an ${\mathscr{G}}$-chain, two $(-1)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves of self-intersections $-2$ joined by a bad tail, a chain of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves on which there is at most one non-reduced singularities, or a non-invariant smooth rational curve with tangency order zero.
\item ($D_n$ type) Two $(-1)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves of self-intersections $-2$ joined by a bad tail which itself connects to a chain of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves on which there are only reduced singularities. 
\item (e.g.l.) Elliptic Gorenstein leaves. That is, either a cycle of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves or a rational curve with only one node. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end thm-15 -->
<!-- rmk-4: body_md -->
Only the eigenvalues of foliation singularities on the chain of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{G}}$-curves can vary in a family.
<!-- end rmk-4 -->
<!-- thm-16: body_md -->
\label{RR}
Let $X$ be a normal complete surface and $D$ be a Weil divisor on $X$. 
Then we have 
\[\chi(D) = \frac{1}{2}D\cdot(D-K_X) + \chi({\mathcal{O}}_X)+\sum_{x\in\textnormal{Sing}(X)} a(x,D)\]
where $a(x,D)$ is a local contribution of ${\mathcal{O}}_X(D)$ at $x$ depending only on the local isomorphism class of the reflexive sheaf ${\mathcal{O}}_X(D)$ at $x$.
<!-- end thm-16 -->
<!-- prop-4: body_md -->
\label{local_contribution}
Let $m$ be a non-negative integer. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $D$ is Cartier at $x$, then $a(x,D)=0$. 
\item If $(X,{\mathscr{F}},x)$ is a mild log canonical non-canonical foliation singularity, then 
\[a(x,mK_{\mathscr{F}}) = 0 \mbox{ for all } m.\]
\item If $(X,{\mathscr{F}},x)$ is a canonical foliation singularity, which is ${\mathbb Q}$-Gorentein but it is not terminal. 
Then we have two cases:
\begin{enumerate}
\item ${\mathscr{F}}$ is Gorenstein and $a(x,mK_{\mathscr{F}}) = 0$ for all $m$.
\item ${\mathscr{F}}$ is $2$-Gorenstein and 
\[a(x,mK_{\mathscr{F}}) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}
0 & \mbox{ for $m$ even} \\
\frac{-1}{2} & \mbox{ for $m$ odd.}
\end{array}\right.\] 
\end{enumerate}
\item If $(X,{\mathscr{F}},x)$ is a canonical foliation singularity and ${\mathscr{F}}$ is not ${\mathbb Q}$-Gorenstein at $x$, then we have 
\[a(x,mK_{\mathscr{F}}) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}
0 & \mbox{ for $m=0$} \\
-1 & \mbox{ for positive $m$.}
\end{array}\right.\] 

\item If $(X,{\mathscr{F}},x)$ is a terminal foliation singularity, then $a(x,K_{\mathscr{F}}) = \frac{1-n}{2n}$ where the surface singularity at $x$ is of the type $\frac{1}{n}(1,q)$ for some $n$ and $q$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end prop-4 -->
<!-- pf-8: body_md -->
(1) follows from the definition. 
(2) follows from (1) since  $K_{\mathscr{F}}$ is Cartier at these foliation singularities. 
(3) is \cite[Proposition 2.4]{hacon2021birational} and (4) is \cite[Proposition 2.6]{hacon2021birational}. 
(5) follows from \cite[Corollary 2.2]{hacon2021birational} and \cite[Example 5.6]{langer2000chern}. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-8 -->
<!-- rmk-5: body_md -->
In addition to any singularities on canonical models, we only allow \emph{mild} log canonical foliation singularities, which have no local contributions by Proposition~\ref{local_contribution}. 
Thus, we have the following similar proposition as \cite[Proposition 4.1]{hacon2021birational} for log canonical models.
<!-- end rmk-5 -->
<!-- prop-5: body_md -->
\label{bdd}
Fix a function $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
There exist constants $B_1$, $B_2$, $B_3$, and $B_4$ such that if $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ is a log canonical model with Hilbert function $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}}) = P(m)$ for all $m\in{\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0}$, then $K_{\mathscr{F}}^2 = B_1$, $K_{\mathscr{F}}\cdot K_X = B_2$, $\chi({\mathcal{O}}_X) = B_3$, and the number of cusp singularities is equal to $B_4$. 
Moreover, there exists some constants $C_1$ and $C_2$ such that the number of terminal and dihedral singularities is at most $C_1$ and the index at any terminal foliation singularity is at most $C_2$.
<!-- end prop-5 -->
<!-- pf-9: body_md -->
The proof follows closely from the proof of \cite[Proposition 4.1]{hacon2021birational}. 
For the reader's convenience, we include the proof. 

By Theorem~\ref{RR}, we have 
\[P(m) = \chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}}) = \frac{1}{2}mK_{\mathscr{F}}\cdot (mK_{\mathscr{F}}-K_X)+\chi({\mathcal{O}}_X)+\sum_{x\in\textnormal{Sing}(X)} a(x,mK_{\mathscr{F}})\]
Since $K_{\mathscr{F}}^2$ is the quadratic term of $P$ and $K_{\mathscr{F}}\cdot K_X$ is the linear term of $P$, both of them are fixed. 
Also $\chi({\mathcal{O}}_X) = P(0)$ is also fixed. 
If we put $m=1$, then we get the number 
\[\sum_{x\in\textnormal{Sing}(X)} a(x,K_{\mathscr{F}})\]
is fixed. 

Let $\Sigma_1$ be the set of terminal foliation singularities, $\Sigma_2$ be the set of dihedral quotient singularities, and $\Sigma_3$ be the set of cusp singularities. 
Also let $\Sigma = \Sigma_1\cup\Sigma_2\cup\Sigma_3$. 
Then by Proposition~\ref{local_contribution}, we have  
\[-\sum_{x\in\textnormal{Sing}(X)} a(x,K_{\mathscr{F}}) = \sum_{x\in\Sigma_1}\frac{n_x-1}{2n_x} + \sum_{x\in\Sigma_2}\frac{1}{2}+\sum_{x\in\Sigma_3}1 \geq \frac{1}{4}\vert\Sigma\vert.\] 
So the number of singularities is bounded and hence 
\[\sum_{x\in\Sigma_1}\frac{1}{n_x} = \vert\Sigma\vert+\vert\Sigma_3\vert+2\sum_{x\in\textnormal{Sing}(X)} a(x,K_{\mathscr{F}})\]
assumes finitely many values. 
By \cite[Lemma 3.4]{hacon2021birational}, the indices at the terminal foliation singularities are bounded by $C_2$. 

Finally, let $m = (2C_2)!$. 
Then by Theorem~\ref{RR} and Proposition~\ref{local_contribution}, we have 
\[P(m) = \chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}}) = \frac{1}{2}mK_{\mathscr{F}}\cdot(mK_{\mathscr{F}}-K_X)+\chi({\mathcal{O}}_X) - \vert\Sigma_3\vert.\]
Hence, the number of cusps is fixed. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-9 -->
<!-- defn-20: body_md -->
\label{mpdvr}
We call $f : (Y,{\mathscr{G}},D) \longrightarrow (X,{\mathscr{F}})$ as above the \emph{minimal partial du Val resolution} of the given log canonical model where $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)$ is a foliated triple (see Definition~\ref{fol_triple}).
<!-- end defn-20 -->
<!-- rmk-6: body_md -->
\label{unique}
If $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)$ is the minimal partial du Val resolution of some log canonical models $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ of general type, then $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ is unique. 
More precisely, if $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)$ is the minimal partial du Val resolution of two log canonical models $(X_1,{\mathscr{F}}_1)$ and $(X_2,{\mathscr{F}}_2)$. 
We have $f_1^*K_{{\mathscr{F}}_1} = K_{\mathscr{G}}+D = f_2^*K_{{\mathscr{F}}_2}$. 
Let $C$ be a curve contracted by $f_1$. 
So we have $f_2^*K_{{\mathscr{F}}_2}\cdot C = f_1^*K_{{\mathscr{F}}_1}\cdot C=0$. 
Since $K_{{\mathscr{F}}_2}$ is numerically ample by Lemma~\ref{ample}, $C$ is also contracted by $f_2$.
<!-- end rmk-6 -->
<!-- defn-21: body_md -->
\label{set_MPdVR}
Fix a function $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
Let ${\mathcal{S}}_P$ be the set of foliated triples $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)$ which are minimal partial du Val resolutions of log canonical models $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ of general type with $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}}) = P(m)$. 
Also let ${\mathcal{S}}_P^C\subset {\mathcal{S}}_P$ be the subset consisting of foliated triples $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},\emptyset)$ which are minimal partial du Val resolutions of canonical models $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ of general type with $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}})=P(m)$.
<!-- end defn-21 -->
<!-- defn-22: body_md -->
\label{family_fol}
Let $\mu: {\mathcal{Y}} \longrightarrow T$ be a projective morphism between two quasi-projective varieties of finite type. We say a foliation ${\mathcal{F}}$ (of rank one) on ${\mathcal{Y}}$ is a family of foliations over $T$ if $\Omega_{{\mathcal{Y}}}^{[**]} \longrightarrow \Omega_{\mathcal{F}}$ factors through the relative hull $\Omega_{{\mathcal{Y}}/T}^{[**]}$ over $T$. 
Here the (relative) hull is defined in \cite[Definition 14 and 17]{kollar2008hulls}.
<!-- end defn-22 -->
<!-- thm-17: body_md -->
\label{key_thm}
The set ${\mathcal{S}}_P$ is bounded. 
More precisely, there exists a projective morphism $\mu : {\mathcal{Y}} \longrightarrow T$ and a family of foliations ${\mathcal{F}}$ on ${\mathcal{Y}}$ over $T$ where ${\mathcal{Y}}$ and $T$ are quasi-projective varieties of finite type such that, for any $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, there is a $t\in T$ and an isomorphism $\rho : Y\longrightarrow {\mathcal{Y}}_t$ such that ${\mathscr{G}}(-D) \cong \rho^*({\mathcal{F}}\vert_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t})$.
<!-- end thm-17 -->
<!-- pf-10: body_md -->
The proof follows closely from the proof of \cite[Theorem 0.1]{chen2021boundedness} for canonical models. 
For the reader's convenience, we include the proof. 
The difference is that now we possibly have non-invariant exceptional divisors $D = \sum D_j$. 

Let $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be the log canonical model of $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)$ (see Remark~\ref{unique}) with the associated morphism $f : (Y,{\mathscr{G}},D) \longrightarrow (X,{\mathscr{F}})$. 
Notice that $f^*K_{\mathscr{F}} = K_{\mathscr{G}}+D$. 
Let $E = \cup E_i$ be the exceptional divisor of $f : Y \longrightarrow X$. 
We divide the proof into several steps.

\begin{enumerate}
\item\label{adjoint_ample} \textit{Claim.} $K_Y+mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)$ is nef (resp. ample) when $m \geq 3$ (resp. $m\geq 4$).
\begin{pf}
Given any irreducible curve $C$ on $Y$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $C=E_i$ for some $i$, then 
\[(K_Y+mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D))\cdot C = K_Y\cdot C > 0\]
since $K_Y$ is ample over $X$. 
\item If $C$ is not contained in the exceptional divisor, then we have two cases: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $K_Y\cdot C\geq 0$, then 
\begin{align*}
(K_Y+mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D))\cdot C &\geq mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)\cdot C \\
&= mi({\mathscr{G}})K_{{\mathscr{F}}}\cdot f_*C > 0 
\end{align*}
since $K_{\mathscr{F}}$ is numerically ample (see Lemma~\ref{ample}). 

\item If $K_Y\cdot C<0$, by \cite[Proposition 3.8]{fujino2012minimal}, every $K_Y$-negative extremal ray is spanned by a rational curve $C$ with $0<-K_Y\cdot C\leq 3$. 
Thus, if we write $C \equiv \sum a_iC_i+B$ where $B\cdot K_Y\geq 0$, the $C_i$'s are $K_Y$-negative extremal rays, the $a_i$'s are non-negative, and at least one of $a_i$ is positive. 
By what we have seen above, we have 
\[(K_Y+mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D))\cdot B\geq 0.\]
Thus, we have 
\begin{align*}
(K_Y+mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D))\cdot C &\geq \sum_ia_i \Big(K_Y\cdot C_i+mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)\cdot C_i\Big) \\
&\geq \sum_ia_i(- 3+m) \geq 0 \mbox{ (resp. $>0$)}.
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}
When $m\geq 4$, we notice that 
\[K_Y+mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D) = K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D) + (m-3)i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)\] 
is big since it is the sum of a nef divisor and a big divisor. 
\end{pf}

\item \textit{Claim.} $i(K_Y)$ and $i({\mathscr{G}})$ are bounded at foliation singularities. 
\begin{pf}
By Proposition~\ref{bdd}, $i(K_Y)$ and $i({\mathscr{G}})$ are bounded in terms of $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}})$ at terminal foliation singularities. Other foliation singularities are at du Val singularities at which ${\mathscr{G}}$ is canonical. Then we have $i(K_Y) = 1$ and $i({\mathscr{G}}) \leq 2$ by Proposition~\ref{local_contribution}(3).
\end{pf}

\item \textit{Claim.} The embedding dimension at each point at which ${\mathscr{G}}$ is singular is bounded. 
\begin{pf}
By Proposition~\ref{bdd}, the index at each point at which ${\mathscr{G}}$ is terminal is bounded in terms of $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}})$. 
Actually, it is shown that the order of each cyclic group acting at each point at which ${\mathscr{G}}$ is terminal is bounded. 
Thus, the embedding dimension at each point at which ${\mathscr{G}}$ is terminal is bounded. 
See for example \cite[Corollary 2.5]{reid2012surface}. 
If the action is $\frac{1}{n}(1,q)$ and $\frac{n}{n-q} = [a_1,\ldots, a_k]$, then the embedding dimension is at most $k+2$. 

Other singularities on $Y$ are du Val singularities, at which the embedding dimensions are $3$. 
\end{pf}
Thus, we have a uniform bound $\delta$ such that $\delta_\zeta\leq\delta$ for $|\zeta|=2$. 
See Remark~\ref{delta}.

\item We consider the ${\mathbb Q}$-Cartier divisor 
\begin{align*}
L &= \alpha i(K_Y)(K_Y+4i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)) - K_Y\\
&= (\alpha i(K_Y)-1)(K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D))+(\alpha i(K_Y)+3)i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D).
\end{align*}

Since $i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)$ is Cartier, 
we can fix an $\alpha$, which only depends on the Hilbert function $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}})$, such that for any irreducible curve $C$, we have 
\begin{align*}
L^2 &\geq (\alpha i(K_Y)+3)^2> \delta \mbox{ and}\\
L\cdot C &\geq \alpha i(K_Y)+3>\delta/2. 
\end{align*}
By Theorem~\ref{va_eff}, $K_Y+\lceil L\rceil = \alpha i(K_Y)(K_Y+ 4i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D))$ separates points and tangents. 
Hence, by Theorem~\ref{sep}, it is very ample.

\item \textit{Claim.} The set of surfaces $X$ where $(X, {\mathscr{F}}) \in {\mathcal{S}}_P$ forms a bounded family.
\begin{pf}
Let $\varphi : Y \longrightarrow {\mathbb P}^N$ be an embedding defined via $|K_Y + L|$. We may assume that $N$ is minimal in the sense that $\varphi(Y)$ is not contained in any hyperplane of ${\mathbb P}^N$. 
In this case, it is known (for a reference, see \cite[Proposition 0]{eisenbud1987varieties}) that 
\[\deg\varphi(Y) \geq 1 + (N-\dim \varphi(Y)) = N-1.\]

By \cite[Lemma 3.5]{hacon2021birational}, we know that $\gamma K_{{\mathscr{F}}}-K_{X}$ is pseudo-effective for 
\[\gamma = \max\left\{\frac{2K_{{\mathscr{F}}}\cdot K_{X}}{K_{{\mathscr{F}}}^2}+3i_{\mathbb Q}({\mathscr{F}}),0\right\}\] 
which is bounded in terms of $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}})$. 
Thus, 
\begin{align*}
\deg\varphi(Y) &= \mbox{{\rm vol}}(K_Y+L) \\
&= \mbox{{\rm vol}}\Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(K_Y+ 4i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D))\Big) \\
&\leq \mbox{{\rm vol}}\Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(K_{X}+ 4i({\mathscr{G}})K_{{\mathscr{F}}})\Big) \\
&\leq \mbox{{\rm vol}}\Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(K_{X}+ 4i({\mathscr{G}})K_{{\mathscr{F}}}) + \alpha i(K_Y)(\gamma K_{{\mathscr{F}}}-K_{X}) \Big) \\
&= \mbox{{\rm vol}}\Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(\gamma + 4i({\mathscr{G}}))K_{{\mathscr{F}}} \Big) \\
&= \Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(\gamma + 4i({\mathscr{G}}))K_{{\mathscr{F}}} \Big)^2
\end{align*}
which is bounded in terms of $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}})$. 
Therefore $N$ is also bounded. 

Hence, by the boundedness result about Chow varieties, we have the boundedness of surfaces $Y$ where $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
\end{pf}

\item Now, we would like to show the boundedness of ${\mathscr{G}}(-D)$. 

We have shown that there exists a projective morphism $\mu : {\mathcal{Y}}\longrightarrow T$ where ${\mathcal{Y}}$ and $T$ are quasi-projective varieties of finite type such that for any $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, there is a $t\in T$ such that ${\mathcal{Y}}_t\cong Y$ and by construction we have 
\[\xymatrix{{\mathcal{Y}} \ar@{^{(}->}[r] \ar[d]_-\mu & {\mathbb P}^N_T \ar[ld] \\ T & }\]
and ${\mathcal{O}}_Y(m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D) + nK_Y) = {\mathcal{O}}_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}(1)$ where $m=4\alpha i(K_Y)i({\mathscr{G}})$ and $n = \alpha i(K_Y)$. 
Note that $\alpha$, $i(K_Y)$, and $i({\mathscr{G}})$ are fixed and determined by the function $P$. 
Without loss of generality, we may assume that $T$ is the closure of $T'$ where 
\[T' = \{t\,\vert\, {\mathcal{Y}}_t\cong Y \mbox{ for some } (Y, {\mathscr{G}}, D)\in {\mathcal{S}}_P\}.\] 

\item We may assume that $T$ is reduced. 
\begin{claim}
We may assume that $T$ is irreducible. 
\end{claim}
\begin{pf}
Let $T = \bigcup_iT_i$ be the decomposition of $T$ into irreducible components. 
If there is a family of pre-foliations ${\mathcal{F}}_i$ on each ${\mathcal{Y}}_i = {\mathcal{Y}}\times_T T_i$ such that for any $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, there exist an $i$ and $t\in T_i$ with $(Y,{\mathscr{G}}(-D))\cong ({\mathcal{Y}}_i,{\mathcal{F}}_i)_t$, then the disjoint union of these families gives the required family. 
\end{pf}

\begin{claim}
We may assume that $T$ is smooth. 
\end{claim}
\begin{pf}
This is achieved by the existence of a finite stratification of $T$ by smooth locally closed subsets. 
\end{pf}

\item Recall that, by Serre's criterion, ${\mathcal{Y}}$ is normal if and only if it is $R_1$ and $S_2$. 
\begin{claim}
We may assume that ${\mathcal{Y}}$ is normal. 
\end{claim}
\begin{pf}
Suppose that ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$ is $R_1$ (resp. $S_2$), then there exists an open subset $U\subset T$ containing $t$ 
such that ${\mathcal{Y}}_U := {\mathcal{Y}}\times_T U$ is $R_1$ (resp. $S_2$) and every fiber ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$ is also $R_1$ (resp. $S_2$) for $t\in U$. 
(For a reference, see \cite[Th\'{e}or\`{e}me 12.2.4]{grothendieck1966elements}.) 
It follows that there is an open subset $V \subset T$ such that ${\mathcal{Y}}_V := {\mathcal{Y}}\times_T V$ is normal, every fiber ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$ is normal for $t\in V$, and for all $Y\in {\mathcal{S}}$, there exists a $t\in V$ such that $Y\cong {\mathcal{Y}}_t$. 
Hence, by shrinking $T$, we may assume that ${\mathcal{Y}}$ is normal. 
\end{pf}

\item \textit{Claim.} We may assume that $K_{\mathcal{Y}}$ is ${\mathbb Q}$-Cartierness. 
\begin{pf}
This is well-known; see, for example, \cite[Lemma 1.27]{simpson1994moduli}. 
We include proof for the convenience of the reader. 

Since ${\mathcal{Y}}$ is normal, the canonical sheaf $K_{\mathcal{Y}}$ is defined as a divisorial sheaf. 
By assumption, $i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}$ is Cartier for 
\[t\in T^\circ := \{t\in T\,\vert\, \mbox{there exists } (Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P \mbox{ such that } {\mathcal{Y}}_t\cong Y\}.\]
Note that $T^\circ$ is a dense subset of $T$. 
For any $t\in T^\circ$, we fix a $d$ such that $i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}(d)$ is generated by global sections. 
Then by replacing $T$ by an open subset, we may assume that the map 
\[\mu_*{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathcal{Y}}(i(K_Y)K_{\mathcal{Y}}(d))\otimes k(t) \longrightarrow H^0({\mathcal{Y}}_t,i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}(d))\]
is surjective by \cite[Theorem 12.8 and Corollary 12.9]{hartshorne1977algebraic}. 
Since $i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}(d)$ is locally generated by some section of $H^0({\mathcal{Y}}_t,i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}(d))$, by lifting this section to a section of $H^0({\mathcal{Y}},i(K_{\mathcal{Y}}) K_{\mathcal{Y}}(d))$ using the surjection above and by Nakayama's lemma, $i(K_Y)K_{\mathcal{Y}}(d)$ is locally generated by one section on a neighborhood of ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$. 
Therefore, $i(K_Y)K_{\mathcal{Y}}$ is Cartier on a neighborhood of ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$. 
Shrinking $T$, we may assume that $i(K_Y)K_{\mathcal{Y}}$ is Cartier. 
\end{pf}

\item Now we consider the function 
\begin{align*}
\Phi(\ell) = {} & \chi(Y,{\mathcal{O}}_X(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D+\ell(m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+nK_Y))) \\
= {} & \chi(X,{\mathcal{O}}_X((m\ell+1)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+n\ell K_Y)) \\
= {} & \frac{1}{2}\Big((m\ell+1)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+n\ell K_Y\Big)\cdot\Big((m\ell+1)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+(n\ell-1)K_Y\Big) \\
& + \chi({\mathcal{O}}_Y) + \sum_{y\in\textnormal{Sing}(Y)}a\big(y,(m\ell+1)(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D)+n\ell K_Y\big) 
\end{align*}
Note that $m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)$ and $nK_Y$ are Cartier, we have that 
\[a\big(y,(m\ell+1)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+n\ell K_Y\big) = a(y,K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)\] 
for any singularity $y\in Y$. 
Also we have
\begin{align*}
\chi({\mathcal{O}}_Y) + \sum_{y\in\textnormal{Sing}(Y)}a(y,K_{\mathscr{G}}+D) 
&= \chi(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D) - \frac{1}{2}(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)\cdot(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D-K_Y) \\
&= P(1) - \frac{1}{2}(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)\cdot(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D-K_Y).
\end{align*}
Thus, we have  
\begin{align*}
\Phi(\ell) = {} & \frac{1}{2}\Big((m\ell+1)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+n\ell K_Y\Big)\cdot\Big((m\ell+1)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+(n\ell-1)K_Y\Big) \\
& + P(1) - \frac{1}{2}(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)\cdot(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D-K_Y)
\end{align*}
is a polynomial with coefficients in terms of $P(1)$, $(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)\cdot K_Y = K_{\mathscr{F}}\cdot K_X$, $(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)^2=K_{\mathscr{F}}^2$, and $K_Y^2$. 
Since the function $P$ is fixed, we have $K_{\mathscr{F}}^2$ and $K_{\mathscr{F}}\cdot K_X$ are fixed by Proposition~\ref{bdd}. 
Moreover, $K_Y^2$ has only finitely many possibilities since the surfaces $Y$ are in a bounded family. 
Therefore, we have finitely many possible polynomials $\Phi(\ell)$. 

Notice that $\frac{m+1}{n-1}>\frac{m}{n} = 4i({\mathscr{G}})\geq 4$. 
So we have $(m+1)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+(n-1)K_Y$ is ample by step~(\ref{adjoint_ample}) and thus $\Phi(1)=h^0(Y,{\mathcal{O}}_Y((m+1)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+nK_Y))$. 

Let $\varphi$ be the maximum of $\Phi(1)$ among all possible polynomials $\Phi(\ell)$. 

\item Applying \cite[Theorem 21]{kollar2008hulls} to the projective morphism $\mu : {\mathcal{Y}} \longrightarrow T$ and the coherent sheaf $\Omega_{{\mathcal{Y}}/T}$, after shrinking $T$ further, we may assume that $\Omega_{{\mathcal{Y}}/T}$ has a relative hull $\Omega_{{\mathcal{Y}}/T}^{[**]} = \Omega_{{\mathcal{Y}}/T}^{**}$. 
Note that the relative hull behaves well under base change. 

For any polynomial $\Psi(\ell) := \Phi(\ell)-s$ where $0\leq s\leq \varphi$, we consider the Quot scheme 
\[Q := \textnormal{Quot}_{\Omega_{{\mathcal{Y}}/T}^{**}/{\mathcal{Y}}/T}^{\Psi(\ell),{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathcal{Y}}(1)},\] 
which is projective over $T$. 
Let ${\mathcal{U}} := {\mathcal{Y}}\times_T Q$. 
Then by a flattening stratification on $Q$, we may assume that the projection morphism ${\mathcal{U}} \longrightarrow Q$ is flat. 
Now by the universal property of Quot schemes, there is a (universal) quotient sheaf ${\mathcal{L}}$ of $\Omega_{{\mathcal{U}}/Q}^{**}$ on ${\mathcal{U}}$. 
Moreover, by \cite[Th\'{e}or\`{e}me 12.2.1 (v)]{grothendieck1966elements}, the loci 
\[\{q\in Q\, : \,{\mathcal{L}}\vert_{{\mathcal{U}}_q} \textnormal{ is torsion-free}\} \textnormal{ and } \{q\in Q\, : \,{\mathcal{L}}^*\vert_{{\mathcal{U}}_q} \textnormal{ is reflexive}\}\]
are open. 
After shrinking $Q$, we may assume that ${\mathcal{L}}$ is torsion-free and ${\mathcal{L}}^*$ is reflexive over any point of $Q$, ${\mathcal{L}}$ is torsion-free, and ${\mathcal{L}}^*$ is reflexive. 
In particular, $\Omega_{{\mathcal{U}}/Q}^{**}\longrightarrow {\mathcal{L}}$ gives a family of foliations on ${\mathcal{U}}$ over $Q$. 

Now for any $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, we dualize the following short exact sequence 
\[\xymatrix{0\ar[r] & {\mathscr{G}} \ar[r] & T_Y \ar[r]^-\tau & T_Y/{\mathscr{G}} \ar[r] & 0}\] 
and get the short exact sequence 
\[\xymatrix{0\ar[r] & (T_Y/{\mathscr{G}})^* \ar[r]^-{\tau^*} & \Omega_Y^{**} \ar[r] & \textnormal{coker}(\tau^*) \ar[r] & 0.}\] 
Note that 
\[\xymatrix{0\ar[r] & \textnormal{coker}(\tau^*)\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_Y(D) \ar[r] & {\mathcal{O}}_Y(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D) \ar[r] & {\mathcal{Z}}\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_Y(D) \ar[r] & 0}\] 
where ${\mathcal{Z}}$ is the sheaf supported at a $0$-dimensional subscheme. 
Notice that $m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+nK_Y$ is ample and Cartier, we have the length of ${\mathcal{Z}}$ is at most 
\begin{align*}
& h^0(Y,{\mathcal{Z}}\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_Y(D+m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+nK_Y)) \\
= {} & \chi(Y,{\mathcal{Z}}\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_Y(D+m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+nK_Y)) \\
\leq {} & h^0(Y,{\mathcal{O}}_Y((m+1)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+nK_Y))\leq\varphi
\end{align*}

Then we have 
\[\chi(Y,{\mathcal{O}}_Y((K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+\ell(m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+nK_Y))) - \chi(Y,\textnormal{coker}(\tau^*)\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_Y(D+\ell(m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+nK_Y)))\]
is a non-negative constant $\leq \varphi$. 
Thus, the function 
\[\chi(Y,\textnormal{coker}(\tau^*)\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_Y(D+\ell(m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)+nK_Y)))\] 
has the form $\Phi(\ell)-s$. 
So by the construction of $Q$, there is a $q\in Q$ such that $\rho : Y \longrightarrow {\mathcal{U}}_q$ is an isomorphism and 
$\textnormal{coker}(\tau^*)\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_Y(D)\cong\rho^*({\mathcal{L}}\vert_{{\mathcal{U}}_q})$ and thus 
\[{\mathscr{G}}(-D) \cong \textnormal{coker}(\tau^*)^*\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_Y(-D) \cong (\textnormal{coker}(\tau^*)\otimes{\mathcal{O}}_Y(D))^*\cong\rho^*({\mathcal{L}}\vert_{{\mathcal{U}}_q})^*.\] 

Notice that $\rho^*({\mathcal{L}}\vert_{{\mathcal{U}}_q})^*$ and $\rho^*({\mathcal{L}}^*\vert_{{\mathcal{U}}_q})$ are isomorphic at the generic point of ${\mathcal{U}}_q$. 
By~\cite[Lemma 1.8]{hacon2021birational}, they are indeed isomorphic. 
Hence, ${\mathcal{L}}^*$ gives the desired family of foliations over $Q$. 
\end{enumerate}
\qed
<!-- end pf-10 -->

since $K_Y$ is ample over $X$. 
\item If $C$ is not contained in the exceptional divisor, then we have two cases:

&\geq \sum_ia_i(- 3+m) \geq 0 \mbox{ (resp. $>0$)}.
\end{align*}

\end{enumerate}
When $m\geq 4$, we notice that 
\[K_Y+mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D) = K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D) + (m-3)i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)\]

Let $\varphi : Y \longrightarrow {\mathbb P}^N$ be an embedding defined via $|K_Y + L|$. We may assume that $N$ is minimal in the sense that $\varphi(Y)$ is not contained in any hyperplane of ${\mathbb P}^N$. 
In this case, it is known (for a reference, see \cite[Proposition 0]{eisenbud1987varieties}) that 
\[\deg\varphi(Y) \geq 1 + (N-\dim \varphi(Y)) = N-1.\]

By \cite[Lemma 3.5]{hacon2021birational}, we know that $\gamma K_{{\mathscr{F}}}-K_{X}$ is pseudo-effective for 
\[\gamma = \max\left\{\frac{2K_{{\mathscr{F}}}\cdot K_{X}}{K_{{\mathscr{F}}}^2}+3i_{\mathbb Q}({\mathscr{F}}),0\right\}\] 
which is bounded in terms of $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}})$. 
Thus, 
\begin{align*}
\deg\varphi(Y) &= \mbox{{\rm vol}}(K_Y+L) \\
&= \mbox{{\rm vol}}\Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(K_Y+ 4i({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D))\Big) \\
&\leq \mbox{{\rm vol}}\Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(K_{X}+ 4i({\mathscr{G}})K_{{\mathscr{F}}})\Big) \\
&\leq \mbox{{\rm vol}}\Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(K_{X}+ 4i({\mathscr{G}})K_{{\mathscr{F}}}) + \alpha i(K_Y)(\gamma K_{{\mathscr{F}}}-K_{X}) \Big) \\
&= \mbox{{\rm vol}}\Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(\gamma + 4i({\mathscr{G}}))K_{{\mathscr{F}}} \Big) \\
&= \Big(\alpha i(K_Y)(\gamma + 4i({\mathscr{G}}))K_{{\mathscr{F}}} \Big)^2
\end{align*}
which is bounded in terms of $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}})$.

Hence, by the boundedness result about Chow varieties, we have the boundedness of surfaces $Y$ where $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$.
