<!-- end claim-2 -->
<!-- pf-15: body_md -->
Let $T = \bigcup_iT_i$ be the decomposition of $T$ into irreducible components. 
If there is a family of pre-foliations ${\mathcal{F}}_i$ on each ${\mathcal{Y}}_i = {\mathcal{Y}}\times_T T_i$ such that for any $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, there exist an $i$ and $t\in T_i$ with $(Y,{\mathscr{G}}(-D))\cong ({\mathcal{Y}}_i,{\mathcal{F}}_i)_t$, then the disjoint union of these families gives the required family.
<!-- end pf-15 -->
<!-- claim-3: body_md -->
We may assume that $T$ is smooth.
<!-- end claim-3 -->
<!-- pf-16: body_md -->
This is achieved by the existence of a finite stratification of $T$ by smooth locally closed subsets.
<!-- end pf-16 -->
<!-- claim-4: body_md -->
We may assume that ${\mathcal{Y}}$ is normal.
<!-- end claim-4 -->
<!-- pf-17: body_md -->
Suppose that ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$ is $R_1$ (resp. $S_2$), then there exists an open subset $U\subset T$ containing $t$ 
such that ${\mathcal{Y}}_U := {\mathcal{Y}}\times_T U$ is $R_1$ (resp. $S_2$) and every fiber ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$ is also $R_1$ (resp. $S_2$) for $t\in U$. 
(For a reference, see \cite[Th\'{e}or\`{e}me 12.2.4]{grothendieck1966elements}.) 
It follows that there is an open subset $V \subset T$ such that ${\mathcal{Y}}_V := {\mathcal{Y}}\times_T V$ is normal, every fiber ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$ is normal for $t\in V$, and for all $Y\in {\mathcal{S}}$, there exists a $t\in V$ such that $Y\cong {\mathcal{Y}}_t$. 
Hence, by shrinking $T$, we may assume that ${\mathcal{Y}}$ is normal.
<!-- end pf-17 -->
<!-- pf-18: body_md -->
This is well-known; see, for example, \cite[Lemma 1.27]{simpson1994moduli}. 
We include proof for the convenience of the reader. 

Since ${\mathcal{Y}}$ is normal, the canonical sheaf $K_{\mathcal{Y}}$ is defined as a divisorial sheaf. 
By assumption, $i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}$ is Cartier for 
\[t\in T^\circ := \{t\in T\,\vert\, \mbox{there exists } (Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P \mbox{ such that } {\mathcal{Y}}_t\cong Y\}.\]
Note that $T^\circ$ is a dense subset of $T$. 
For any $t\in T^\circ$, we fix a $d$ such that $i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}(d)$ is generated by global sections. 
Then by replacing $T$ by an open subset, we may assume that the map 
\[\mu_*{\mathcal{O}}_{\mathcal{Y}}(i(K_Y)K_{\mathcal{Y}}(d))\otimes k(t) \longrightarrow H^0({\mathcal{Y}}_t,i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}(d))\]
is surjective by \cite[Theorem 12.8 and Corollary 12.9]{hartshorne1977algebraic}. 
Since $i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}(d)$ is locally generated by some section of $H^0({\mathcal{Y}}_t,i(K_Y)K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}(d))$, by lifting this section to a section of $H^0({\mathcal{Y}},i(K_{\mathcal{Y}}) K_{\mathcal{Y}}(d))$ using the surjection above and by Nakayama's lemma, $i(K_Y)K_{\mathcal{Y}}(d)$ is locally generated by one section on a neighborhood of ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$. 
Therefore, $i(K_Y)K_{\mathcal{Y}}$ is Cartier on a neighborhood of ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$. 
Shrinking $T$, we may assume that $i(K_Y)K_{\mathcal{Y}}$ is Cartier.
<!-- end pf-18 -->
<!-- rmk-7: body_md -->
After some stratification on $Q$, we have $({\mathcal{Y}},{\mathcal{G}},{\mathcal{D}}) \longrightarrow Q$ is a family of foliated triples (see Defition~\ref{defn_fol_family}) for some reduced divisor ${\mathcal{D}}$.
<!-- end rmk-7 -->
<!-- lem-6: body_md -->
\label{nef_big_open}
Let ${\mathcal{X}} \longrightarrow T$ be a flat family of projective varieties of dimension $n$ and $D$ is a ${\mathbb Q}$-Cartier divisor on ${\mathcal{X}}$ and flat over $T$. 
If there is a $t_0\in T$ such that $D_{t_0}$ is nef (resp. strictly nef) and big, then there exists an open subset $U\subset T$ containing $t_0$ such that $D_t$ is nef (resp. strictly nef) and big for all $t\in U$. 
Moreover, there exists an $N$ such that $h^0({\mathcal{X}}_t,ND_t)\geq 1$ for all $t\in T$.
<!-- end lem-6 -->
<!-- pf-19: body_md -->
We may assume that $T$ is irreducible. 
Indeed, suppose the lemma holds whenever $T$ is irreducible. 
In general, we write $T = \bigcup_{j=1}^mT^j$ as the decomposition of irreducible components $T^j$. 
Since $t_0\in T$, we have $t_0\in T^j$ for some $j$. 
Let us say $t_0\in T^1$. 
By the assumption, we have an open subset $U^1\subset T^1$ containing $t_0$ such that $D_t$ is nef (resp. strictly nef) and big for all $t\in U^1$. 
If $U^1$ is contained in $T\setminus\bigcup_{j=2}^mT^j$ which is an open subset of $T$, then $U^1$ is an open subset of $T$ and we are done. 
If not, there is a point $t_1\in U^1\cap\bigcup_{j=2}^m T^j \subset \bigcup_{j=2}^m T^j$. 
By induction on the number of the irreducible components of $T$, we have an open subset $U^2\subset \bigcup_{j=2}^m T^j$ containing $t_1$ such that $D_t$ is nef (resp. strictly nef) and big for all $t\in U^2$. 
Note that $C^1 := T^1\setminus U^1$ and $C^2 := \bigcup_{j=2}^mT^j\setminus U^2$ are closed subsets of $T$. 
Thus $U := T\setminus(C^1\cup C^2)$ is an open subset of $T$ containing $t_0$ such that $D_t$ is nef (resp. strictly nef) and big for all $t\in U$. 

So from now on, we assume that $T$ is irreducible. 
Since $D_{t_0}$ is nef, we have $D_{t}$ is nef for very general $t\in T^* = T\setminus\bigcup_{i=1}^\infty T_i$ where $T_i$'s are all proper closed subsets of $T$. 
(For a reference, see \cite[Proposition 1.4.14]{lazarsfeld2004positivity}.)
Note that, for all $t\in T^*$, we have $D_t^n = D_{t_0}^n>0$ since $D_{t_0}$ is nef and big.
Hence, $D_t$ is also nef and big for all $t\in T^*$. 

Let $S_N := \{t\in T\vert\, h^0({\mathcal{X}}_t,ND_{t})\geq 1\}$ which is a closed subset in $T$ by the upper semi-continuity. 
Note that we have \[T({\mathbb C}) = \left(\bigcup_N S_N({\mathbb C})\right)\cup\left(\bigcup_i T_i({\mathbb C})\right).\] 

By the Baire category theorem, there is an $N$ such that $S_N = T$. 
Thus, the relative base locus of $D$ is proper. 
Let $U$ be an open subset of $T$ such that all irreducible components of the relative base locus of $D$ are flat over $U$. 
Notice that it is possible that $t_0$ is \emph{not} in $U$. 

Now for any $u\in U$, if there is a curve $C_u$ such that $D_u\cdot C_u<0$ (resp. $\leq 0$), then $C_u$ is in the relative base locus of $D$ and moves in the family over $U$. 
So for any $t\in T^*\cap U$, we have $D_t\cdot C_t = D_u\cdot C_u < 0$ (resp. $\leq 0$), which is a contradiction. 
Therefore, $D_u$ is nef (resp. strictly nef) for all $u\in U$.  
Moreover, $D_u^n = D_{t}^n >0$ where $t\in T^*\cap U$, then $D_u$ is also big for $u\in U$. 

If $t_0\in U$, then we are done. 
If not, that is $t_0\in T\setminus U$, then by induction on $\dim T$, there exists an open subset $V\subset T\setminus U$ containing $t_0$ such that $D_t$ is nef (resp. strictly nef) and big for all $t\in V$. 
So $(T\setminus U)\setminus V$ is a closed subset of $T\setminus U$, which is a closed subset of $T$. 
Thus, $(T\setminus U)\setminus V$ is a closed subset of $T$. 
Therefore $V\cup U = T\setminus\big((T\setminus U)\setminus V\big) \subset T$ is an open subset containing $t_0$ such that $D_t$ nef (resp. strictly nef) and big for all $t\in V\cup U$.
\qed
<!-- end pf-19 -->
<!-- cor-2: body_md -->
\label{trivial_move}
Every $(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)$-trivial curve moves in the family over $U$.
<!-- end cor-2 -->
<!-- prop-6: body_md -->
\label{dihedral_bdd}
Fix a function $P:{\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
There exist constants $C_1$, $C_2$, and $C_3$ such that, for any log canonical model $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ with Hilbert function $\chi(X,mK_{{\mathscr{F}}})=P(m)$, the index (resp. embedding dimension) at the dihedral singularities is at most $C_1$ (resp. $C_2$) and the number of dihedral singularities is at most $C_3$. 
Moreover, there exist constants $B_1$, $B_2$, and $B_3$ such that the index (resp. embedding dimension) at the non-terminal foliation singularities which are cyclic quotient singularities is at most $B_1$ (resp. $B_2$) and the number of non-terminal foliation singularities which are cyclic quotient singularities is at most $B_3$.
<!-- end prop-6 -->
<!-- pf-20: body_md -->
The proof follows closely from the proof of \cite[Proposition 3.1]{chen2021boundedness} for canonical models. 
For the reader's convenience, we include the proof. 

By Theorem~\ref{key_thm}, there exists a projective morphism $\mu : {\mathcal{Y}}\longrightarrow T$ of quasi-projective varieties of finite type and a family of foliations ${\mathcal{F}}$ on ${\mathcal{Y}}$ over $T$ such that for any $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, there exists a $t\in T$ and an isomorphism $\rho:Y\longrightarrow {\mathcal{Y}}_t$ such that ${\mathscr{G}}(-D)\cong \rho^*({\mathcal{F}}\vert_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t})$. 
We may assume that 
\[T^* :=\{t\in T\,\vert\, ({\mathcal{Y}}_t,{\mathcal{F}}_t)\cong (Y,{\mathscr{G}}(-D)) \mbox{ for some } (Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P\}\] 
is dense in $T$. 
Fix a $t_0\in T^*$. 

Note that $K_{\mathcal{F}}\vert_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}$ is nef and big, by Lemma~\ref{nef_big_open}, we have that $K_{\mathcal{F}}$ is big over $T$. 
Thus, the relative base locus of $K_{\mathcal{F}}$ is proper. 
Therefore, we have a finite stratification of $T$ such that all irreducible components of the relative base locus of $K_{\mathcal{F}}$ are flat over $T$. 

Let ${\mathcal{E}}_j$'s be those irreducible components of the relative base locus of $K_{\mathcal{F}}$ over $U$ of codimension one. 
Note that, for any $t\in T^*$ and for any irreducible curve $E\subset {\mathcal{Y}}_t$ with $K_{\mathcal{F}}\cdot E = 0$, we have $E$ is in the relative base locus of $D$ and hence $E\subset{\mathcal{E}}_j$ for some $j$. 
Let $\pi:\widetilde{{\mathcal{Y}}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal{Y}}$ be the log resolution of $({\mathcal{Y}},\sum_j{\mathcal{E}}_j)$ with the exceptional divisors $\sum {\mathcal{F}}_\ell$. 
By shrinking $T$ further, we may assume that $\nu := \mu\circ \pi$ is smooth and ${\mathcal{F}}_\ell$ is flat over $T$. 
Let $\widetilde{{\mathcal{E}}_j}$ be the proper transform of ${\mathcal{E}}_j$ via $\pi$. 

Note that $\Lambda := \{\widetilde{{\mathcal{E}}_j}, {\mathcal{F}}_\ell\}$ is a finite set. 
So there are only finitely many possible connected subsets of $\Lambda$ with dual graphs of $D_n$ type or $A_n$ type. 
By \cite[Satz 2.9 and Satz 2.11]{brieskorn1968rationale}, the intersection matrix of a dihedral singularity determines the embedding dimension and the group acting on it. 
Since the intersection matrix remains the same in the family, we have the boundedness of the embedding dimension and the order of the group acting on these singularities. 
Hence the index of $X$ at the dihedral singularities is also bounded. 
Similarly, by \cite{reid2012surface}, the embedding dimension and the index of a cyclic quotient singularity is determined by the intersection matrix. 
Therefore, we have the boundedness of the embedding dimension and of the index at the cyclic quotient singularities. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-20 -->
<!-- rmk-8: body_md -->
\begin{enumerate}
\item It is possible that some connected subset of $\Lambda$ of $D_n$ type or of $A_n$ type is redundant. 
\item By the same argument as above, we also show the boundedness of the cusps. 
Precisely, the number of exceptional divisors and the intersection matrix over any cusp singularity are bounded. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end rmk-8 -->
<!-- thm-18: body_md -->
\label{bir}
Fix a function $P: {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
There exists an integer $m_P$ such that if $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ is a log canonical model of general type and $\chi(mK_{\mathscr{F}})=P(m)$ for all $m\geq 0$, then for any $m>0$ divisible by $m_P$, $|mK_{\mathscr{F}}|$ defines a birational map which is an isomorphism on the complement of the cusp singularities.
<!-- end thm-18 -->
<!-- pf-21: body_md -->
This follows closely from \cite[Theorem 4.3]{hacon2021birational}. 
See also \cite[Theorem 3.3]{chen2021boundedness}. 
For the reader's convenience, we include the proof. 

Let $g : (Y,{\mathscr{G}}) \longrightarrow (X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be the minimal resolution of cusps. 
Then $K_{\mathscr{G}} = g^*K_{\mathscr{F}}$ and $i({\mathscr{G}})=i_{\mathbb Q}({\mathscr{F}})$. (See Definition~\ref{index}.)
\begin{claim}
$K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}}$ is nef. 
\end{claim}
\begin{pf}[Claim]
Given any irreducible curve $C$ on $Y$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $C$ is contracted by $g$, then 
\[(K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot C = K_Y\cdot C = -2-C^2 \geq 0\]
since $C^2\leq -2$ by the minimality of $g$. 
\item If $C$ is not contracted by $g$, 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $K_Y\cdot C\geq 0$, then 
\[(K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot C \geq 3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{{\mathscr{F}}}\cdot g_*C > 0\] 
by Lemma~\ref{ample}.

\item If $K_Y\cdot C<0$, by \cite[Proposition 3.8]{fujino2012minimal}, every $K_Y$-negative extremal ray is spanned by a rational curve $C$ with $0<-K_Y\cdot C\leq 3$. 
Thus, if we write $C \equiv \sum a_iC_i+D$ where $D\cdot K_Y\geq 0$, the $C_i$'s are $K_Y$-negative extremal rays, the $a_i$'s are non-negative, and at least one of $a_i$ is positive. 
By what we have seen above, $(K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot D\geq 0$. 
Thus, 
\begin{align*}
& (K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot C \\
= {} & \sum_ia_i \Big((K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot C_i\Big) + (K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot D \\
\geq {} & \sum_ia_i(- 3+3) + 0 = 0.
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}
This completes the proof of the nefness of $K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}}$. 
\end{pf}

Now, by \cite[Lemma 3.5]{hacon2021birational}, we know that $\gamma K_{\mathscr{G}}-K_Y$ is big for any fixed integer $\gamma$ with 
\[\gamma > \left\lceil\max\left\{\frac{2K_{{\mathscr{F}}}\cdot K_{X}}{K_{{\mathscr{F}}}^2}+3i_{\mathbb Q}({\mathscr{F}}),0\right\}\right\rceil.\]

Note that $L := (\beta-\gamma)K_{\mathscr{G}}+(\gamma K_{\mathscr{G}}-K_Y)$ is pseudo-effective for any $\beta>\gamma$.
Let $L=P+N$ be the Zariski decomposition. 
Then we have 
\[P^2\geq(\beta-\gamma)^2K_{\mathscr{G}}^2\geq \left(\frac{\beta-\gamma}{i_{\mathbb Q}({\mathscr{F}})}\right)^2.\]
And if $C$ is not in the exceptional divisor of $g$, then 
\[P\cdot C\geq (\beta-\gamma)K_{\mathscr{G}}\cdot C\geq \frac{\beta-\gamma}{i_{\mathbb Q}({\mathscr{F}})}.\]

By Proposition~\ref{dihedral_bdd} and Proposition~\ref{bdd}, we have the boundedness of embedding dimension of each rational singularity on $Y$. 
Thus, we have a uniform bound $\delta$ such that $\delta_\zeta\leq\delta$ for $|\zeta|=2$. 
Now we fix a $\beta$ divisible by $i_{\mathbb Q}({\mathscr{F}})$ such that $P^2>\delta$ and $P\cdot C>\delta/2$ for any irreducible curve $C$. 
By \cite[Theorem 0.1]{langer2001adjoint} and Proposition~\ref{sep}, we have that $K_Y+L = \beta K_{\mathscr{G}}$ is very ample on the complement of the exceptional divisor of $g$. 
By \cite[Theorem 6.2]{sakai1984weil}, $g_*{\mathcal{O}}_Y(\beta K_{\mathscr{G}}) = {\mathcal{O}}_X(\beta K_{\mathscr{F}})$. 
Hence, $\beta K_{\mathscr{F}}$ is very ample on the complement of the cusps.
\qed
<!-- end pf-21 -->
<!-- claim-5: body_md -->
$K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}}$ is nef.
<!-- end claim-5 -->
<!-- pf-22: body_md -->
Given any irreducible curve $C$ on $Y$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $C$ is contracted by $g$, then 
\[(K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot C = K_Y\cdot C = -2-C^2 \geq 0\]
since $C^2\leq -2$ by the minimality of $g$. 
\item If $C$ is not contracted by $g$, 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $K_Y\cdot C\geq 0$, then 
\[(K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot C \geq 3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{{\mathscr{F}}}\cdot g_*C > 0\] 
by Lemma~\ref{ample}.

\item If $K_Y\cdot C<0$, by \cite[Proposition 3.8]{fujino2012minimal}, every $K_Y$-negative extremal ray is spanned by a rational curve $C$ with $0<-K_Y\cdot C\leq 3$. 
Thus, if we write $C \equiv \sum a_iC_i+D$ where $D\cdot K_Y\geq 0$, the $C_i$'s are $K_Y$-negative extremal rays, the $a_i$'s are non-negative, and at least one of $a_i$ is positive. 
By what we have seen above, $(K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot D\geq 0$. 
Thus, 
\begin{align*}
& (K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot C \\
= {} & \sum_ia_i \Big((K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot C_i\Big) + (K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}})\cdot D \\
\geq {} & \sum_ia_i(- 3+3) + 0 = 0.
\end{align*}
\end{enumerate} 
\end{enumerate}
This completes the proof of the nefness of $K_Y+3i({\mathscr{G}})K_{\mathscr{G}}$.
<!-- end pf-22 -->
<!-- defn-23: body_md -->
\label{defn_fol_family}
Fix $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0}\longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
We call $\pi : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta) \longrightarrow B$ \emph{a family of foliated triples} (see also Definition~\ref{fol_triple}) if 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\pi : {\mathcal{X}}\longrightarrow B$ is a projective morphism such that all fibers are surfaces with at worst semi-log canonical singularities. (For a reference, see~\cite[Definition 3.13.5]{hacon2010classification}.)
\item ${\mathcal{F}}$ is a foliation of rank 1 on ${\mathcal{X}}$ such that ${\mathcal{F}}$ is tangent to the fibers of $\pi$, that is, ${\mathcal{F}}$ is a family of foliations on ${\mathcal{X}}$ over $B$. (See Definition~\ref{family_fol}.)
\item $\Delta = \sum\Delta_i$ is a reduced divisor with all $\Delta_i$'s flat over $B$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-23 -->
<!-- defn-24: body_md -->
\label{defn_moduli}
Fix an integral-valued function $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item A triple $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D)$ is called \emph{${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable} if the followings hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X = \cup_iX_i$ is a surface with at worst semi-log canonical singularities where $X_i$'s are irreducible. 
\item ${\mathscr{F}}$ is a pre-foliation on $X$. 
\item $D$ is a Weil divisor on $X$. 
\item There exists a flat projective ${\mathbb Q}$-Gorenstein (that is, both $K_{\mathcal{X}}$ and $K_{\mathcal{F}}$ are ${\mathbb Q}$-Cartier) one-parameter family of foliated triples $\pi : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta) \longrightarrow C$ such that, for some point  $0\in C$, the restriction on the fiber over the point $c\in C\setminus\{0\}$ is in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$ and the restriciton on the fiber ${\mathcal{X}}_0$ over $0$ is $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D)$, that is, $X\cong{\mathcal{X}}_0$, ${\mathcal{F}}\vert_{{\mathcal{X}}_0}\cong{\mathscr{F}}$, and $\Delta\vert_{{\mathcal{X}}_0}=D$. 
\item $({\mathcal{F}},\Delta)$ and $({\mathcal{F}}_{X_i},\Delta_{X_i})$ are log canonical for all $i$ where ${\mathcal{F}}_{X_i}$ is the restricted foliation and $K_{{\mathcal{F}}_{X_i}}+\Delta_{X_i} = (K_{\mathcal{F}}+\Delta)\vert_{X_i}$. 
\end{enumerate}

\item An ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable triple $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D)$ is called \emph{stable} if $\Omega_{\mathcal{F}}(\Delta)\vert_X$ is nef and 
\[\left(\left(\omega_{\mathcal{X}}\otimes(\Omega_{\mathcal{F}}(\Delta))^{4i(P)}\right)^{**}\right)\vert_X\] 
is ample where $\pi : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)\longrightarrow C$ is a flat projective ${\mathbb Q}$-Gorenstein one-parameter family of foliated triples as in  (1)(d).
(See Lemma~\ref{iP} for the definition of $i(P)$.)

\item A family of \emph{stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable} foliated triples over a scheme $B$ is a family of foliated triples $\pi : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta) \longrightarrow B$ over $B$ such that, for any $b\in B$, 
\begin{enumerate}
\item the fiber $(Y,{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)_b$ is a \emph{stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable} foliated triple, 
\item $\omega_{{\mathcal{X}}/B}^{[\ell]}\vert_{{\mathcal{X}}_b}\cong \omega_{{\mathcal{X}}_b}^{[\ell]}$ for all $\ell\in{\mathbb Z}$, and
\item $(\Omega_{{\mathcal{F}}}(\Delta))^{[\ell]}\vert_{{\mathcal{X}}_b}\cong (\Omega_{{\mathcal{F}}}(\Delta)\vert_{{\mathcal{X}}_b})^{[\ell]}$ for all $\ell\in{\mathbb Z}$ where $(\bullet)^{[\ell]} = ((\bullet)^{\otimes \ell})^{**}$. 
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end defn-24 -->
<!-- rmk-9: body_md -->
In particular, any foliated triples $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)$ in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$ are stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable. 
Indeed, we consider $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ the log canonical model of $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)$ (see Remark~\ref{unique}) and $f : (Y,{\mathscr{G}},D) \longrightarrow (X,{\mathscr{F}})$ the associated morphism. 
In the proof of Theorem~\ref{key_thm}, we have shown that $K_{\mathscr{G}}+D = f^*K_{\mathscr{F}}$ which is nef and $K_Y+mi({\mathscr{G}})(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)$ is ample for $m\geq 4$.
<!-- end rmk-9 -->
<!-- rmk-10: body_md -->
Let $X$ be a surface of a threefold. 
Given any log canonical foliated triple $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D)$ of rank one. 
For any proper birational morphism $\pi : Y \longrightarrow X$, we have 
\[K_{{\mathscr{F}}_Y}+\pi_*^{-1}D+F = \pi^*(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D)+E\]
where $E$ and $F$ are effective exceptional divisors and $F$ is reduced by \cite[Lemma 8.2]{cascini2020mmp}. 
The \emph{pullback foliated triple} is defined to be $(Y,{\mathscr{F}}_Y,\pi_*^{-1}D+F)$. 
In particular, we have $\pi_*(K_{{\mathscr{F}}_Y}+\pi_*^{-1}D+F) = K_{\mathscr{F}}+D$.
<!-- end rmk-10 -->
<!-- defn-25: body_md -->
\label{functor}
We define the moduli functor ${\mathcal{M}}_P^{\textnormal{sm}} :  \textnormal{(Schemes)} \longrightarrow \textnormal{(Sets)}$ by sending the scheme $B$ to the sets of isomorphism classes of \emph{stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable} foliated triples over $B$.
<!-- end defn-25 -->
<!-- lem-7: body_md -->
\label{iP}
Fix a function $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
Then there exists an $i(P)\in{\mathbb N}$ depending only on $P$ such that $i(P)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)$ is Cartier for all $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$.
<!-- end lem-7 -->
<!-- pf-23: body_md -->
We can take $i(P) = C_2!$ where $C_2$ comes from Proposition~\ref{bdd} and depends only on $P$. \qed
<!-- end pf-23 -->
<!-- thm-19: body_md -->
\label{inv}
Fix a function $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
Given any family of foliated triples $f : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)\longrightarrow T$ where $T$ is connected and $({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)_t\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$ for all $t\in T$ (see Definition~\ref{defn_fol_family} for families of foliated triples), there exists an $m_{f}$ depending only on this family $f$ such that  
\[h^0({\mathcal{X}}_t,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}}+\Delta)\vert_{{\mathcal{X}}_t})\] 
is independent of $t$ for $m\geq m_f$ and divisible by $i(P)$. (See Lemma~\ref{iP}.)
<!-- end thm-19 -->
<!-- pf-24: body_md -->
The idea of the proof is from the proof of \cite[Proposition 3.7]{cascini2018invariance}. 
We divide the proof into the following steps. 
Let $m\in{\mathbb N}$ be a positive integer divisible by $i(P)$. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item Fix a point $0\in T$ and let $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D) := ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)\vert_{{\mathcal{X}}_0}\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
Let $\rho : X^{\textnormal{m}} \longrightarrow X$ be the minimal resolution of $X$ and ${\mathscr{F}}^{\textnormal{m}}$ be the pullback foliation on $X^\textnormal{m}$. 
Contracting down all ${\mathscr{F}}^{\textnormal{m}}$-chains to get $(Y,{\mathscr{G}})$, we have a morphism $\pi: (Y,{\mathscr{G}}) \longrightarrow (X,{\mathscr{F}})$. 
\[\xymatrix{X^{\textnormal{m}}  \ar[dd]_-\rho \ar[rd] & \\ & Y \ar[ld]^-\pi \\ X &}\]
Let $E$ be the proper transform of $D$. 
Thus, because of the construction of the minimal partial du Val resolution (\ref{mpdvr}), we have $K_{\mathscr{G}}+E = \pi^*(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D)$, which is nef and big.  

Let $\Gamma_1$, $\ldots$, $\Gamma_p$ be all elliptic Gorenstein leaves on $Y$ and $C_1$, $\ldots$, $C_q$ be all disconnected chains of rational curves \emph{exceptional over its log canonical model} such that $(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E)\cdot C_j^{(k)}=0$ where $C_j = \sum_{k=1}^{r_j} C_j^{(k)}$ is the sum of its irreducible components. 
Also let $Z = \sum_{i=1}^p\Gamma_i + \sum_{j=1}^q C_j$. 

\item \textit{Claim.} $h^1(\Gamma_i,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E))=0$ for all $i$.
\begin{pf}
Notice that $\Gamma_i$ is Cohen-Macaulay with the trivial dualizing sheaf. 
Since each irreducible component of $E$ is over a log canonical non-canonical foliation singularity, $E$ does not meet $\Gamma_i$. 
So we have 
\[h^1(\Gamma_i, m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)) = h^0(\Gamma_i,-m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)) = h^0(\Gamma_i,-mK_{{\mathscr{G}}}) = 0\]
where the last equality is because ${\mathcal{O}}_{\Gamma_i}(mK_{{\mathscr{G}}})$ is not torsion and has degree 0 by \cite[FactIII.0.4 and Theorem IV.2.2]{mcquillan2008canonical}.
\end{pf}

\item \textit{Claim.} $h^1(C_j,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E))=0$ for all $j$.
\begin{pf}
Note that we have  
\[(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E)\cdot C_j^{(k)}=0\]
for all $j$ and $k$. 
Since $C_j^{(k)}$'s are either smooth rational curves or a rational curve with two singularities of index two, we have 
\begin{equation}\label{h1_van}
h^1(C_j^{(k)},m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E)) = 0
\end{equation}
for all $j$ and $k$. 
Now, for any fixed $j$, we consider the following short exact sequence 
\[\xymatrix{0 \ar[r] & {\mathcal{O}}_{C_j} \ar[r] & \displaystyle \bigoplus_{k=1}^{r_j}{\mathcal{O}}_{C_j^{(k)}} \ar[r] & \displaystyle \bigoplus_{k=1}^{r_j-1}{\mathcal{O}}_{C_j^{(k)}\cap C_j^{(k+1)}} \ar[r] & 0.}\]
Tensoring with ${\mathcal{O}}_{C_j}(m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E))$ and taking the induced long exact sequence, we notice that the map 
\[\xymatrix{\displaystyle \bigoplus_{k=1}^{r_j}H^0\big({C_j^{(k)}},m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E)\big) \ar[r] & \displaystyle \bigoplus_{k=1}^{r_j-1}H^0\big({C_j^{(k)}\cap C_j^{(k+1)}},m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E)\big)}\]
is surjective and thus, we have that $h^1(C_j,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E))=0$ for all $j$ by equation~(\ref{h1_van}). 
\end{pf}

\item \textit{Claim.} $h^j(Y, m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)-Z)=0$ for $j>0$ and for all $m\geq m_0$ for some $m_0$. 
\begin{pf}
For any irreducible curve $C$ in the support of $Z$, we have that 
\[\big(m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)-(K_Y+Z)\big)\cdot C = -(K_Y+Z)\cdot C\geq 0.\]
Note that $K_{\mathscr{G}}+E = \pi^*(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D)$ is nef and big, and the $(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E)$-trivial curves are exactly the curves in the support of $Z$.
Then there exists an $m_0$ depending only on $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D)$ such that $m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)-(K_Y+Z)$ is nef and big for $m\geq m_0$. 
Since $Y$ is klt, we have 
\[h^j(Y,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)-Z) = h^j(Y,K_Y+m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)-(K_Y+Z)) = 0\]
for all $j>0$ and $m\geq m_0$ by Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing theorem. 
\end{pf}

\item \textit{Claim.} $h^j(Y,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E))=0$ for $j>0$ and for all $m\geq m_0$. 
\begin{pf}
By steps (2) and (3), we have that $h^1(Z,m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E)) = 0$. 
Now we consider the short exact sequence 
\[\xymatrix{0 \ar[r] & {\mathcal{O}}_Y(-Z) \ar[r] & {\mathcal{O}}_Y \ar[r] & {\mathcal{O}}_Z \ar[r] & 0.}\]
Tensoring with ${\mathcal{O}}_Y(m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E))$ and taking the induced long exact sequence, we have the map
\[\xymatrix{H^1(Y,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)-Z) \ar[r] & H^1(Y,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E))}\]
is surjective and $H^2(Y,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)-Z) \cong H^2(Y,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E))$. 
Thus, we have $h^j(Y,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E)) = 0$ for $j>0$ and for all $m\geq m_0$ by step (4). 
\end{pf}

\item \textit{Claim.} $h^1(X,m(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D))=0$ for all $m\geq m_0$. 
\begin{pf}
Note that $\pi_*(m(K_{\mathscr{G}}+E)) = m(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D)$ by the projection formula. 
Since $h^1(Y,m(K_{{\mathscr{G}}}+E))=0$ for all $m\geq m_0$ by step (5), we have that 
\[h^1(X,m(K_{{\mathscr{F}}}+D))=0\] 
for all $m\geq m_0$ by Leray spectral sequence. 
\end{pf}

\item \textit{Claim.} $h^2({\mathcal{X}}_t,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t))=0$ for all $t\in T$ and for $m\geq m_P$ for some $m_P$. 
\begin{pf}
Note that $K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t$ is nef and big since $({\mathcal{X}}_t,{\mathcal{F}}_t,\Delta_t)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$.  
In addition, we have already seen, in the proof of Theorem~\ref{key_thm}, that $K_{{\mathcal{X}}_t}+4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t)$ is ample. 
Moreover, by \cite[Lemma 3.5]{hacon2021birational}, we have that $m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t) - K_{{\mathcal{X}}_t}$ is big for $m\geq m_P$ where 
\[m_P := \max\left\{\frac{2(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t)\cdot K_{{\mathcal{X}}_t}}{(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t)^2}+4i(P)+1, 1\right\}.\]
By Proposition~\ref{bdd}, we have that $m_P$ depends only on $P$. 

Now by Serre duality, we have, for $m\geq m_P$, that 
\[h^2({\mathcal{X}}_t,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t)) = h^0({\mathcal{X}}_t,K_{{\mathcal{X}}_t} - m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t)) = 0\] 
since there is no section for an anti-big divisor. 
\end{pf}

\item Take $m_f := \max\{m_0, m_P\}$ which only depends on the family $f$. 
Now we have, for all $t\in T$ and for all $m\geq m_f$, that  
\begin{align*}
h^0({\mathcal{X}}_t,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t)) &\geq \chi({\mathcal{X}}_t,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t)) \\
&= \chi({\mathcal{X}}_0,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_0}+\Delta_0)) \\
&= h^0({\mathcal{X}}_0,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_0}+\Delta_0))
\end{align*}
where the first inequality comes from step (7) and the last equality comes from steps (6) and (7). 

On the other hand, by upper semi-continuity, we have 
\[h^0({\mathcal{X}}_t,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t))\leq h^0({\mathcal{X}}_0,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_0}+\Delta_0)).\]
Therefore, we get the desired equality. 
\qed
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end pf-24 -->

<!-- rmk-11: body_md -->
\label{h_vanishing}
The arguments above also show that $h^1({\mathcal{X}}_t,m(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t)) = 0$ for $m\geq m_f$ and divisible by $i(P)$.
<!-- end rmk-11 -->
<!-- cor-3: body_md -->
Fix a function $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
There is an $m_P$ depending only on $P$ such that, for all $m\geq m_P$ and divisible by $i(P)$, we have that 
\[h^1(X,m(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D))=h^2(X,m(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D))=0\] and 
$h^0(X,m(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D))$ is constant for all $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$.
<!-- end cor-3 -->
<!-- pf-31: body_md -->
By Theorem~\ref{key_thm} and \ref{open}, we have finitely many families $f_j$'s of foliated triples parametrizing ${\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
Taking $m_P$ divisible by all $m_{f_j}$'s in Theorem~\ref{inv}, we have 
\[h^1(X,m(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D)) = h^2(X,m(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D)) = 0\] 
for all $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
Since $\chi(X,m(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D))$ is constant for all $(X,{\mathscr{F}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, so is $h^0(X,m(K_{\mathscr{F}}+D))$. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-31 -->
<!-- defn-26: body_md -->
\label{elementary}
Let $X$ be a smooth variety, ${\mathscr{F}}$ be a foliation of rank 1 on $X$, and $p$ be a singularity of ${\mathscr{F}}$. 
Let $v$ be a germ of a vector field around $p$ associated to ${\mathscr{F}}$. 
Then $p$ is called \emph{elementary} if $v$ has a non-zero non-nilpotent linear part.
<!-- end defn-26 -->
<!-- rmk-12: body_md -->
Elementary singularities are log canonical by \cite[Fact I.ii.4]{mcquillan2013almost}.
<!-- end rmk-12 -->
<!-- thm-20: body_md -->
\label{line_rsln}
Any germ of vector fields on $({\mathbb C}^3,0)$ tangent to a rank-two foliation can be desingularized. 
That is, there exists a finite sequence of blowups such that the pullback foliation has only elementary singularities.
<!-- end thm-20 -->
<!-- defn-27: body_md -->
\label{dlt}
Let $X$ be a normal variety, $B$ an effective ${\mathbb Q}$-divisor, and $f: X\longrightarrow C$ a non-constant morphism to a smooth curve $C$. 
We say that $f : (X,B) \longrightarrow C$ is a \emph{divisorial log terminal} (dlt) if the pair $(X,B+f^{-1}(c))$ is dlt for every closed point $c\in C$.
<!-- end defn-27 -->
<!-- thm-21: body_md -->
\label{KF_MMP}
Let $f : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta) \longrightarrow T$ be a family of foliated triples which is a semi-stable reduction of a family of foliated triples whose general fiber is in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
Then the relative $(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\Delta)$-minimal model program exists and stops with a family of foliated triples $({\mathcal{X}}^{\textnormal{m}},{\mathcal{F}}^{\textnormal{m}},\Delta^{\textnormal{m}}) \longrightarrow T$ such that $(K_{{\mathcal{F}}^{\textnormal{m}}}+\Delta^{\textnormal{m}})$ is nef over $T$, $f^{\textnormal{m}} : {\mathcal{X}}^{\textnormal{m}} \longrightarrow T$ is dlt, and the general fiber is in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$.
<!-- end thm-21 -->
<!-- pf-32: body_md -->
Let $R$ be a $(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\Delta)$-negative extremal ray over $T$. 
Then its locus is not the whole space ${\mathcal{X}}$ since the general fiber of $f$ is a model of a foliated triple in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
Thus, by the proof of \cite[Theorem 8.8]{cascini2020mmp}, we may run the $(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\Delta)$-MMP over $T$, which will end up with a family of foliated triples $({\mathcal{X}}^{\textnormal{m}},{\mathcal{F}}^{\textnormal{m}},\Delta^{\textnormal{m}}) \longrightarrow T$ such that $K_{{\mathcal{F}}^{\textnormal{m}}}+\Delta^{\textnormal{m}}$ is nef over $T$. 
Moreover, $f^{\textnormal{m}} : {\mathcal{X}}^{\textnormal{m}} \longrightarrow T$ is dlt and the general fiber is in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-32 -->
<!-- thm-22: body_md -->
\label{properness}
Let $T$ be a smooth curve and $({\mathcal{X}}^\circ,{\mathcal{F}}^\circ,\Delta^\circ)\in{\mathcal{M}}_P^{\textnormal{sm}}(T^\circ)$ be a family of stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable foliated triples over $T^\circ$ where $T^\circ = T\setminus\{0\}$ and $0\in T$. 
Suppose the fiber of the family over $t\neq 0$ is in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
Then there exists a smooth curve $C$ and a finite morphism $C \longrightarrow T$ such that, after the base change via $C \longrightarrow T$, the pullback family $({\mathcal{X}}_C^\circ,{\mathcal{F}}_C^\circ,\Delta_C^\circ)$ extends uniquely to a family of stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable foliated triples $({\mathcal{X}}_C,{\mathcal{F}}_C,\Delta_C)$ over $C$.
<!-- end thm-22 -->
<!-- pf-33: body_md -->
Let $g : ({\mathcal{Y}},{\mathcal{G}},\Theta) \longrightarrow C$ be a semi-stable reduction of the closure of the family $f^\circ : ({\mathcal{X}}^\circ,{\mathcal{F}}^\circ,\Delta^\circ) \longrightarrow T^\circ$ where $C \longrightarrow T$ is a finite morphism and $C$ is a smooth curve. 

Then by Theorem~\ref{KF_MMP}, we run the relative $(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)$-MMP over $C$. 
Thus, we get a family $g : ({\mathcal{Y}},{\mathcal{G}},\Theta) \longrightarrow C$ such that $K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta$ is nef over $C$. 
By running additional partial $K_{\mathcal{Y}}$-MMP over $C$, we may assume that $K_{\mathcal{Y}}+4i(P)(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)$ is nef over $C$. 
(See Lemma~\ref{iP} for the definition of $i(P)$.)
Note that $\big(K_{\mathcal{Y}}+4i(P)(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)\big)-K_{\mathcal{Y}}$ is nef and big over $C$. 
By relative base point free theorem (see \cite[Theorem 3.24]{kollar1998birational} for a reference), $K_{\mathcal{Y}}+4i(P)(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)$ is semi-ample over $C$. 
Thus, we have the relative canonical model $g : ({\mathcal{Y}},{\mathcal{G}},\Theta) \longrightarrow C$. 

Let $f^\circ_C$ be the base change of $f^\circ$ via the morphism $C^\circ \longrightarrow T^\circ$ where $C^\circ = C\setminus\{0\}$. 
Notice that for any $c\in C\setminus\{0\}$, the fibers of $f^\circ_C$ and $g$ over $c$ are isomorphic. 
Moreover, for $c=0$, we have that $(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)\vert_{{\mathcal{Y}}_0}$ is nef and $K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_0}+4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{G}}}+\Theta)\vert_{{\mathcal{Y}}_0}$ is ample. 
Hence, the fiber of $g$ over $0\in C$ is stable and ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable. 
Therefore, $g : ({\mathcal{Y}},{\mathcal{G}},\Theta) \longrightarrow C$ is a family of stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable foliated triples over $C$. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-33 -->
<!-- thm-23: body_md -->
\label{separatedness}
Let $T$ be a smooth curve, $T^\circ = T\setminus\{0\}$ where $0\in T$, and $({\mathcal{X}}_i,{\mathcal{F}}_i,\Delta_i) \in{\mathcal{M}}_P^{\textnormal{sm}}(T)$ be two families of stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable foliated triples over $T$ for $i=1$, $2$. 
Then any isomorphism $\varphi^\circ : ({\mathcal{X}}_1,{\mathcal{F}}_1,\Delta_1)_{T^\circ} \longrightarrow ({\mathcal{X}}_2,{\mathcal{F}}_2,\Delta_2)_{T^\circ}$ over $T^\circ$ extends uniquely to an isomorphism $\varphi : ({\mathcal{X}}_1,{\mathcal{F}}_1,\Delta_1) \longrightarrow ({\mathcal{X}}_2,{\mathcal{F}}_2,\Delta_2)$ over $T$.
<!-- end thm-23 -->
<!-- lem-8: body_md -->
Fix a function $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
For any $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, we have 
\[Y \cong \textnormal{Proj}\bigoplus_{m\geq 0} H^0(Y,m(K_Y+4i(P)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)))\] 
where $i(P)$ is defined in Lemma~\ref{iP}.
<!-- end lem-8 -->
<!-- pf-34: body_md -->
Notice that $K_Y+4i(P)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D)$ is ample by the part (1) of the proof of Theorem~\ref{key_thm}. \qed
<!-- end pf-34 -->
<!-- lem-9: body_md -->
\label{sep_lc}
Fix a function $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
For any $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$ and any resolution of singularities $f : Z \longrightarrow Y$, we write 
\[K_Z+4i(P)\left(K_{\mathscr{H}}+f_*^{-1}D+\sum_j\varepsilon(E_j)E_j\right) = f^*(K_Y+4i(P)(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D))+\sum_j a_jE_j\] 
where ${\mathscr{H}}$ is the pullback foliation on $Z$ and $E_j$'s are exceptional divisors of $f$. 
Then we have $a_j > -1$ for all $j$ where $\varepsilon(E_j) = 0$ if $E_j$ is ${\mathscr{H}}$-invariant and $\varepsilon(E_j)=1$ otherwise.
<!-- end lem-9 -->
<!-- pf-35: body_md -->
Let $(X,{\mathscr{F}})$ be the log canonical model of $(Y,{\mathscr{G}},D)$. 
Note that $K_{\mathscr{G}}+D$ is the pullback of $K_{\mathscr{F}}$. 
Thus the divisor $K_{\mathscr{H}}+f_*^{-1}D+\sum_j\varepsilon(E_j)E_j - f^*(K_{\mathscr{G}}+D) = \sum_ja'_jE_j$ is effective and exceptional since ${\mathscr{F}}$ has at worst log canonical singularities. 
Moreover, since $Y$ has at worst klt singularities, we have $K_Z - f^*K_Y = \sum_j a''_jE_j$ where $a''_j > -1$. 
Hence, $a_j = 4i(P)a'_j+a''_j > -1$. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-35 -->
<!-- lem-10: body_md -->
\label{adjunction}
Fix a function $P : {\mathbb Z}_{\geq 0} \longrightarrow {\mathbb Z}$. 
Let $T$ be a smooth affine curve and $({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)\in{\mathcal{M}}_P^{\textnormal{sm}}(T)$ be a family of stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable foliated triples over $T$. 
Suppose the fiber of the family over $t\neq 0$ is in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$. 
Assume there is a birational morphism $g : {\mathcal{Y}} \longrightarrow {\mathcal{X}}$ such that $f\circ g : {\mathcal{Y}} \longrightarrow T$ is 
a semi-stable reduction of $({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)$. 
Let ${\mathcal{G}}$ be the pullback foliation of ${\mathcal{F}}$ and $\Theta$ be the proper transform of $\Delta$. 
We may write
\[K_{\mathcal{Y}}+4i(P)(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta) = g^*\big(K_{\mathcal{X}}+4i(P)(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\Delta)\big) + \sum_i a_iE_i + \sum_j b_jF_j\]
where $E_i$ are all exceptional divisors mapping to $0\in T$ and $F_j$ are all exceptional divisors flat over $T$. 
Then $a_i\geq 0$ for all $i$ and $b_j\geq -1$ for all $j$.
<!-- end lem-10 -->
<!-- pf-36: body_md -->
Restriction the equality to the general element $t\in T$, not $0$, we have 
\[K_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}+4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{G}}}+\Theta)\vert_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t} = g_t^*\big(K_{{\mathcal{X}}_t}+4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_t}+\Delta_t)\big) + \sum_j b_jF_j.\]
By Lemma~\ref{sep_lc}, we have, for all $j$, that $b_j\geq -1$. 

Moreover, let $X$ be an irreducible component of ${\mathcal{X}}_0$ and $Y$ be the proper transform of $X$ in ${\mathcal{Y}}$. 
Note that $(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)\vert_{Y} - g_0^*(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\Delta)\vert_{X}$ is effective since $({\mathcal{F}},\Delta)$ is a family of stable ${\mathcal{S}}_P$-smoothable foliated triples where $g_0$ is the morphism from $Y$ to $X$. 
Moreover, by adjunction, we have 
\begin{align*}
& \Big(\sum_i(a_i-1)E_i + \sum_j b_jF_j\Big)\vert_{Y} \\
= {} & \Big(K_{\mathcal{Y}}+Y+4i(P)(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta) - g^*\big(K_{\mathcal{X}}+X+4i(P)(K_{\mathcal{F}}+\Delta)\big)\Big\vert_{Y} \\
\geq {} & K_{Y} - g_0^*K_{X} \\
\geq {} & -\sum_iE_i\vert_{Y} - \sum_j F_j\vert_{Y}
\end{align*}
where the last inequality follows from ${\mathcal{X}}_0$ has semi-log canonical singularities. 
Hence, $a_i\geq 0$ for all $i$. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-36 -->
<!-- pf-37: body_md -->
Let ${\mathcal{Y}}$ be a common resolution of $({\mathcal{X}}_1,\Delta_1)$, $({\mathcal{X}}_2,\Delta_2)$, and $\varphi^\circ$. 
Let $g_1$ and $g_2$ be the morphisms fitting into the following commutative diagram. 
\[\xymatrix{ & {\mathcal{Y}} \ar[ld]_-{g_1} \ar[rd]^-{g_2} & \\
{\mathcal{X}}_1 \ar[rd]_-{f_1} \ar@{-->}[rr]^-{\varphi^\circ} & & {\mathcal{X}}_2 \ar[ld]^-{f_2} \\
 & T & }\]

Note that $g_1^*{\mathcal{F}}_1$ and $g_2^*{\mathcal{F}}_2$ are isomorphic over $T^\circ$, so they are isomorphic at the generic point of ${\mathcal{Y}}$. 
By \cite[Lemma 1.8]{hacon2021birational}, they are in fact isomorphic. 
Let ${\mathcal{G}} = g_1^*{\mathcal{F}}_1 = g_2^*{\mathcal{F}}_2$. 
Moreover, we have the proper transforms $(g_{1*})^{-1}\Delta_1$ and $(g_{2*})^{-1}\Delta_2$ are the same. 
Then we put $\Theta = (g_{1*})^{-1}\Delta_1 = (g_{2*})^{-1}\Delta_2$. 

As in subsection~\ref{ss_reduction}, we may assume that $({\mathcal{Y}},{\mathcal{G}},\Theta) \longrightarrow T$ is a semi-stable reduction. 
Note that ${\mathcal{X}}_1$ and ${\mathcal{X}}_2$ may not be normal after base change. 

Suppose first that ${\mathcal{X}}_1$ is normal. 
We write 
\[K_{{\mathcal{Y}}} + 4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{G}}}+\Theta) = g_1^*\big(K_{{\mathcal{X}}_1}+4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_1}+\Delta_1)\big) + \sum_i a_iE_i + \sum_j b_jF_j\]
where $E_i$ are exceptional divisors mapping to $0\in T$ and $F_j$ are flat over $T$. 

Now, by Lemma~\ref{adjunction}, $a_i\geq 0$, and $b_j\geq -1$. 
Also, by adjunction formula, we notice that 
\begin{align*}
& (g_1)_*\left(K_{{\mathcal{Y}}} + 4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{G}}}+\Theta)+\sum_j F_j\right) \\ 
= {} & (g_1)_*\left(g_1^*\big(K_{{\mathcal{X}}_1}+4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_1}+\Delta_1)\big) + \sum_i a_iE_i + \sum_j (b_j+1)F_j\right) \\
= {} & K_{{\mathcal{X}}_1}+4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_1}+\Delta_1).
\end{align*}
Hence, we have 
\begin{align*}
{\mathcal{X}}_1 &\cong \mbox{{\rm Proj \!}}\bigoplus_{m\geq 0} H^0({\mathcal{X}}_1,m(K_{{\mathcal{X}}_1}+4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{F}}_1}+\Delta_1))) \\
&= \mbox{{\rm Proj \!}}\bigoplus_{m\geq 0} H^0\left({\mathcal{Y}},m\left(K_{{\mathcal{Y}}} + 4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{G}}}+\Theta)+\sum_j F_j\right)\right). 
\end{align*}

If ${\mathcal{X}}_1$ is not normal, then using the same argument as above, we have the normalization 
\[{\mathcal{X}}_1^\nu \cong \mbox{{\rm Proj \!}}\bigoplus_{m\geq 0} H^0\left({\mathcal{Y}},m\left(K_{{\mathcal{Y}}} + 4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{G}}}+\Theta)+\sum_j F_j\right)\right). \]
Note that the conductor of the normalization ${\mathcal{X}}_1^\nu \longrightarrow {\mathcal{X}}_1$ is in the support of $\sum F_j$. 
Thus we have 
\[{\mathcal{X}}_1^\nu \cong \mbox{{\rm Proj \!}}\bigoplus_{m\geq 0} H^0\left({\mathcal{Y}},m\left(K_{{\mathcal{Y}}} + 4i(P)(K_{{\mathcal{G}}}+\Theta)+\sum_j F_j\right)\right) \cong {\mathcal{X}}_2^\nu.\]
Therefore ${\mathcal{X}}_1$ and ${\mathcal{X}}_2$ are isomorphic in codimension 1 where ${\mathcal{X}}_1$ and ${\mathcal{X}}_2$ here are the original one (before taking a base change).  
Since they both satisfy Serre's condition $S_2$, they are, in fact, isomorphic. 

Now we put ${\mathcal{X}}_1\cong{\mathcal{X}}_2\cong{\mathcal{X}}$.
Notice that ${\mathcal{F}}_1$ and ${\mathcal{F}}_2$ are isomorphic at the generic point of ${\mathcal{X}}$. 
So they are indeed isomorphic. 
Moreover, $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_2$ are isomorphic as well. 
\qed
<!-- end pf-37 -->
<!-- lem-11: body_md -->
\label{-2string}
Let ${\mathscr{F}}$ be a foliation with only log canonical singularities on a smooth surface $X$. 
Given a Hirzebruch-Jung string $\bigcup_{i=1}^{s}E_i$ of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{F}}$-curves. 
Assume that there are at most two foliation singularities on each $E_i$. 
Then, after re-indexing, we have that $E_1$ has one or two singularities and $E_i$ has exactly two singularities for $i=2$, $\ldots$, $s$. 
Moreover, let $p_{i-1}$ and $p_{i}$ be the singularities on $E_i$ for $i=2$, $\ldots$, $s$ where $p_i$ is the intersection of $E_i$ and $E_{i+1}$ for $i=2$, $\ldots$, $s-1$. 
(See Figure~\ref{fig_neg2}.)
Then we have the following two cases: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $E_1$ has only one singularity $p_1$, then $p_1$ is a saddle-node and, for $i\geq 2$, $p_i$ is a reduced and non-degenerate singularity with eigenvalue uniquely determined by $E_2^2$, $\ldots$, $E_s^2$. 
\item If $E_1$ has two singularities $p_0$ and $p_1$, then there is at most one $i\in\{0,\ldots, s\}$ such that $p_i$ is not reduced. 
Moreover, if $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_i,p_i)$ (resp. $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_{i+1},p_i)$) is non-positive, then $p_{i-1}$ (resp. $p_{i+1}$) is a saddle-node. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end lem-11 -->
<!-- pf-38: body_md -->
Since ${\mathscr{F}}$ is log canonical, by \cite[Fact I.ii.4]{mcquillan2013almost} the vector field around any fixed point either is a smooth point or belongs to one of three cases in Lemma~\ref{lem_ZCS}. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $E_1$ has only one singularity $p_1$, we have that 
\[\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_1,p_1)=\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_1)=2.\] 
Thus by Lemma~\ref{lem_ZCS}, we know that $p_1$ is a saddle-node, $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_2,p_1) = 1$, and $\textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},E_2,p_1)=0$. 
By Camacho-Sad formula (Theorem~\ref{thm_CS_formula}), we have that 
\[\lambda_2 := \textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},E_2,p_2) = E_2^2-\textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},E_2,p_1) =E_2^2\leq -2. \]
Hence $p_2$ is reduced and non-degenerate. 

\begin{claim}
For all $i=2$, $\ldots$, $s$, $\lambda_i := \textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},E_{i},p_{i})$ are negative rational numbers less than $-1$ and $p_{i}$ are reduced non-degenerate singularities. 
\end{claim}

We have seen that the claim holds for $i=2$. 
Now we assume that $p_i$'s are reduced and non-degenerate with $\lambda_i\in{\mathbb Q}_{<-1}$ for $i=2$, $\ldots$, $k-1$. 
Then we have that $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_k,p_{k-1})=1$ and $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_k,p_k)=1$. 
By Camacho-Sad formula (Theorem~\ref{thm_CS_formula}) and Lemma~\ref{lem_ZCS}, we have that 
\begin{align*}
\lambda_k &= E_k^2-\textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},E_k,p_{k-1}) \\
&= E_k^2-\frac{1}{\lambda_{k-1}} <  -2+1=-1.
\end{align*}
Therefore, by induction, we complete the proof of the claim and of the first case. 

\item Now we assume that all $E_i$'s have two foliation singularities. 
Suppose there are two non-reduced singularities $p_i$ and $p_j$. 
As the proof of Lemma~\ref{pos_rat}, after a sequence of blowups, we get a string with two separatrices at each singularity, which is impossible by Theorem~\ref{separatrix}. 

Moreover, if $\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_i,p_i)\leq 0$, then 
\[\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_i,p_{i-1}) = 2-\textnormal{Z}({\mathscr{F}},E_i,p_i)\geq 2.\]
So, by Lemma~\ref{lem_ZCS}, we have that $p_{i-1}$ is a saddle-node. 
\qed
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end pf-38 -->
<!-- claim-6: body_md -->
For all $i=2$, $\ldots$, $s$, $\lambda_i := \textnormal{CS}({\mathscr{F}},E_{i},p_{i})$ are negative rational numbers less than $-1$ and $p_{i}$ are reduced non-degenerate singularities.
<!-- end claim-6 -->
<!-- lem-12: body_md -->
\label{egl}
Let ${\mathscr{F}}$ be a foliation with only log canonical singularities on a smooth surface $X$. 
Given a cycle $E = \bigcup_{i=1}^{s}E_i$ of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{F}}$-curves where $s\geq 2$. 
Then all singularities on $E$ are reduced and non-degenerate.
<!-- end lem-12 -->
<!-- pf-39: body_md -->
\begin{enumerate}
\item If there is only one non-reduced singularity $p$, then we can view this cycle as one Hirzebruch-Jung string of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{F}}$-curves with 2 non-reduced singularities. 
Thus by Lemma~\ref{-2string}, it is impossible. 

\item If there are more than two non-reduced singularities, then we can take any Hirzebruch-Jung string of $(-2)$-${\mathscr{F}}$-curves such that both endpoints are non-reduced. 
Then by Lemma~\ref{-2string}, it is impossible. 

\item Now we know that all singularities on $E$ are reduced. 
Since all $E_i$'s are $(-2)$-${\mathscr{F}}$-curves, we have that all singularities on $E$ are non-degenerate by Lemma~\ref{lem_ZCS}. 
\end{enumerate}
\qed
<!-- end pf-39 -->
<!-- lem-13: body_md -->
\label{eigenvalue}
Let $\pi:({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}}) \longrightarrow T$ be a smooth family such that 
\begin{enumerate}
\item each irreducible component of foliation singularities is finite over $T$ and pairwise disjoint, and 
\item ${\mathcal{F}}_t$ has at worst log canonical singularities for all $t\in T$. 
\end{enumerate}
Given any irreducible component $W$ of singularities of ${\mathcal{F}}$, we can define a holomorphic function $\lambda : W \longrightarrow {\mathbb P}^1$ such that $\lambda(w)$ is the eigenvalue of ${\mathcal{F}}_{\pi(w)}$ at $w$.
<!-- end lem-13 -->
<!-- pf-40: body_md -->
For any $w\in W$, we can pick an \'{e}tale open subset ${\mathcal{U}}$ of ${\mathcal{X}}$ containing $w$ such that $(x,y,t)$ are local coordinates of ${\mathcal{U}}$ with $\pi(x,y,t) = t$ and $W\cap {\mathcal{U}} = (x=y=0)$. 

Then, on ${\mathcal{U}}$, the foliation is given by 
\[\big(a(t)x+b(t)y+\textnormal{h.o.t.}\big)\frac{\partial}{\partial x}+\big(c(t)x+d(t)y+\textnormal{h.o.t.}\big)\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\]
where $a$, $b$, $c$, and $d$ are holomorphic functions from $\pi(V)$ to ${\mathbb C}$ and h.o.t stands for higher order terms (in $x$, $y$, and $t$). 
Thus we form a matrix 
\[A(t) := \left(\begin{matrix}
a(t) & b(t) \\ c(t) & d(t)
\end{matrix}\right)\]
which has two eigenvalues $\mu_+(t)$ and $\mu_-(t)$. 
Since all foliation singularities are log canonical, at least one of two eigenvalues is not zero. 
Therefore, we can define a holomorphic map $\lambda : W\cap{\mathcal{U}} \longrightarrow {\mathbb P}^1$ by 
$\lambda(w) = [\mu_+(\pi(w)):\mu_-(\pi(w))]$. 
Notice that this map is independent of the open subset ${\mathcal{U}}$ and of change of coordinates. 
Thus, $\lambda$ can be defined on $W$ and is holomorphic. \qed
<!-- end pf-40 -->
<!-- thm-24: body_md -->
\label{open}
Given a family of foliated triples $f : ({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)\longrightarrow T$. 
($T$ is not necessarily a curve.) 
Assume that there is a dense subset $T'\subset T$ such that $({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)_t\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$ for all $t\in T'$. 
(See Definition~\ref{set_MPdVR} and Definition~\ref{defn_fol_family}.) 
Then there exists an open subset $U\subset T$ such that all fibers of $f$ over $U$ are in ${\mathcal{S}}_P$.
<!-- end thm-24 -->
<!-- pf-41: body_md -->
We divide the proof into several steps. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item Let $g: {\mathcal{Y}}\longrightarrow{\mathcal{X}}$ be a resolution of singularities, ${\mathcal{G}} = g^*{\mathcal{F}}$ be the pullback foliation, and $\Theta$ be the proper transform of $\Delta$. 
Let $\pi = f\circ g$. 
By Proposition~\ref{ve_Sei}, replacing ${\mathcal{Y}}$ with its higher model (via some blowups), we may assume that ${\mathcal{Y}}_t$ is smooth and ${\mathcal{G}}_t$ has at worst log canonical singularities for all $t\in U$ for some open subset $U\subset T$. 

\item \textit{Claim.} After shrinking $U$ further if necessary, the following conditions hold: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\pi_U$ is smooth. 
\item Each irreducible component of singularities of ${\mathcal{G}}$ is finite over $U$ and pairwise disjoint. 
\item Each irreducible component of exceptional divisors of $g$ is flat over $U$. 
\item For any irreducible component $C$ of singularities of ${\mathcal{G}}$ and any irreducible component $E$ of exceptional divisors of $g$, we have $C\cap E$ is either $C$ or empty. 
\item For each irreducible component $E$ of exceptional divisors of $g$, either $E_u$ is invariant for all $u\in U$ or $E_u$ is not invariant for all $u\in U$. 
\end{enumerate}
\begin{pf}
More explicitly, (a) comes from the generic smoothness. 
For others, let \[S_1 = \bigcup \pi(C)\] 
where the union is taken over all irreducible components $C$ of singularities of ${\mathcal{G}}$ and of exceptional divisors of $g$, which are \emph{not} finite over $U$. 
Let \[S_2 = \bigcup \{t\,\vert\,C_{i,t} = C_{j,t}\}\] 
where the union is taken over all distinct irreducible components $C_i$ and $C_j$ of singularities of ${\mathcal{G}}$. 
Let \[S_3 = \bigcup\pi(C\cap E)\] 
where the union is taken over all irreducible components $C$ of singularity of ${\mathcal{G}}$ and all irreducible components $E$ of exceptional divisors of $g$ such that $C\cap E$ is neither $C$ nor empty. 

Note that $S_1$, $S_2$, and $S_3$ are all proper closed subsets of $U$. 
So by replacing $U$ by $U\setminus (S_1\cup S_2\cup S_3)$, conditions (a)-(d) hold. 
The condition (e) can be achieved since being non-invariant is an open condition. 
\end{pf}

\item The conditions (a)-(d) will ensure that the number of foliation singularities on an exceptional prime divisor of $g$ is constant over $U$. 
Furthermore, all singularities of ${\mathcal{G}}$ do not collide over $U$. 
Also there is a $t_0\in T'\cap U$ since $T'$ is dense in $T$. 

\item We say an irreducible component $E$ of exceptional divisors a \emph{relative ${\mathcal{G}}$-exceptional curve} if $E_{t_0}$ is a ${\mathcal{G}}_{t_0}$-exceptional curve. 
Then, for any $u\in U$, we have that $E_u$ is invariant, and the contraction of $E_u$ introduces a log canonical foliation singularity on a smooth surface point. 

Contracting all relative ${\mathcal{G}}$-exceptional curves, we may assume that there is no relative ${\mathcal{G}}$-exceptional curve by induction on Picard number. 

\item\label{G-chain} 
Now we say $E=\bigcup_{i=1}^{s}E_i$ is a \emph{relative $({\mathcal{G}},\Theta)$-chain} if $E_{t_0} = \bigcup_{i=1}^{s}E_{i,t_0}$ is a ${\mathcal{G}}_{t_0}$-chain and $E_{i,t_0}\cdot\Theta_{t_0}=0$ for $i=1$, $\ldots$, $s$. 
(See Figure~\ref{fig_chain}.)

\begin{figure}[h]
\begin{tikzpicture}
\def.5{.5}
\filldraw (-.5,-0.5*.5) -- (0,0) -- (3*.5,1.5*.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.25cm] {$p_1$} -- (4*.5,2*.5);
\filldraw (2*.5,2*.5) -- (3*.5,1.5*.5) -- (6*.5,0) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.25cm] {$p_2$} -- (7*.5,-0.5*.5);
\filldraw (5*.5,-0.5*.5) -- (6*.5,0) -- (9*.5,1.5*.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.25cm] {$p_3$} -- (10*.5,2*.5);
\filldraw (8*.5,2*.5) -- (9*.5,1.5*.5) -- (12*.5,0*.5) circle (2pt) -- (13*.5,-0.5*.5);
\draw (15*.5,0.75*.5) node {$\ldots$};
\filldraw (17*.5,-0.5*.5) -- (18*.5,0*.5) circle (2pt)  -- (21*.5,1.5*.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.25cm] {$p_{s-1}$} -- (22*.5,2*.5);
\filldraw (20*.5,2*.5) -- (21*.5,1.5*.5) -- (24*.5,0*.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.25cm] {$p_s$} -- (25*.5,-0.5*.5);
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{An ${\mathscr{F}}$-chain. The straight lines indicate invariant divisors and the solid circles indicate all reduced singularities on these curves.}\label{fig_chain}
\end{figure}

Since, over $t_0$, there is only one singularity $p_{1,t_0}$ on $E_{1,t_0}$, we have that, over any $u\in U$, there is also only one singularity $p_{1,u}$ on $E_{1,u}$. 

By Camacho-Sad formula (Theorem~\ref{thm_CS_formula}), we have $\textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{1,u},p_{1,u}) = E_{1,u}^2\leq -2$. 
And by Lemma~\ref{lem_ZCS}, the eigenvalue $\lambda_1 = \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{1,u},p_{1,u})$ must be a negative integer less than $-2$. 
Thus, $p_{1,u}$ is a reduced non-degenerate singularity. 

Let the singularities on $E_{k,u}$ be $p_{k-1,u}$ and $p_{k,u}$ for $k = 2$, $\ldots$, $s$. 
\begin{claim}
For all $k=1$, $\ldots$, $s$, $\lambda_k := \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{k,u},p_{k,u})$ are negative rational numbers less than $-1$ and $p_{k,u}$ are reduced non-degenerate singularities. 
\end{claim}
\begin{pf}
We have shown that this holds when $k=1$. 
Assume the claim holds for $k-1$. 
By Camacho-Sad formula (Theorem~\ref{thm_CS_formula}) and Lemma~\ref{lem_ZCS}, we have that 
\[-2\geq E_{k,u}^2 = \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{k,u}, p_{k-1,u})+\textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{k,u},p_{k,u}) = \frac{1}{\lambda_{k-1}} + \lambda_{k}. \]
Thus, $\lambda_k\leq -2-\frac{1}{\lambda_{k-1}}<-2+1=-1$. 
Hence, $\lambda_k$ is a negative rational number less than $-1$. 
Therefore, $p_{k,u}$ is also a reduced non-degenerate singularity. 
This completes the proof of the claim. 
\end{pf}

\item We contract all relative $({\mathcal{G}},\Theta)$-chains and still using the notation $({\mathcal{Y}},{\mathcal{G}},\Theta)$ for the resulting foliation. 
Then we have a family such that 
\[(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)\vert_{{\mathcal{Y}}_t}\] 
is nef and big for all $t\in T'\cap U$. 
By Lemma~\ref{nef_big_open}, after shrinking $U$ further, we have $(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)\vert_{{\mathcal{Y}}_u}$ is nef and big for all $u\in U$. 

Next, in order to show that $({\mathcal{Y}},{\mathcal{G}},\Theta)_t\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$, we will study the \emph{relative $(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)$-trivial curves}, that is, the irreducible component $E$ of exceptional divisors such that $E_{t_0}$ is $(K_{{\mathcal{G}}_{t_0}}+\Theta_{t_0})$-trivial.  

\item Let $E = E_{0,1}\cup E_{0,2}\cup\bigcup_{i=1}^s E_i$ be the exceptional divisor over a \emph{dihedral singularity} where, for all $u\in U$,  
$\bigcup_{i=1}^sE_{i,u}$ is a Hirzebruch-Jung string, and $E_{0,1,u}$ and $E_{0,2,u}$ are disjoint, of self-intersection $-2$ and both intersect the bad tail $E_{1,u}$. 
(See the Figure~\ref{fig_dual_Dn} for its dual graph.)

\begin{figure}[h]
\begin{tikzpicture}
\def.5{2}
\filldraw (-.707*.5,.707*.5) circle (2pt) node[left] {$E_{0,1}$} -- (0,0) circle (2pt) node[above] {$E_1$}  -- (.5,0) circle (2pt) node[above] {$E_2$};
\filldraw (-.707*.5,-.707*.5) circle (2pt) node[left] {$E_{0,2}$} -- (0,0);
\draw (1.5*.5,0) node {......};
\filldraw (2*.5,0) circle (2pt) node[above] {$E_{s-1}$} -- (3*.5,0) circle (2pt) node[above] {$E_s$};
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{Dual graph of a $\textnormal{D}_n$ type singularity}\label{fig_dual_Dn}
\end{figure}

Let $p_{0,1,u}$, $p_{0,2,u}$, and $p_{1,u}$ be three singularities on $E_{1,u}$. 
Let $p_{k-1,u}$ and $p_{k,u}$ be two singularities on $E_{k,u}$ for $k = 2$, $\ldots$, $s$. 
(See the Figure~\ref{fig_Dn}.)

\begin{figure}[h]
\begin{center}
\begin{tikzpicture}
\def.5{.6}
\draw (.5,-0.5*.5) -- (-4*.5,2*.5);
\filldraw (-2*.5,0) -- (-.5,0.5*.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.15cm] {$p_{0,2}$} -- (.5,1.5*.5);
\filldraw (-3*.5,0.5*.5) -- (-2*.5,.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.15cm] {$p_{0,1}$}  -- (0,2*.5);
\filldraw (-.5,-0.5*.5) -- (0,0) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.15cm] {$p_1$}  -- (3*.5,1.5*.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.15cm] {$p_2$} -- (4*.5,2*.5);
\filldraw (2*.5,2*.5) -- (6*.5,0) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.15cm] {$p_3$} -- (7*.5,-0.5*.5);
\filldraw (5*.5,-0.5*.5) -- (9*.5,1.5*.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.15cm] {$p_4$} -- (10*.5,2*.5);
\filldraw (8*.5,2*.5) -- (10*.5,.5);
\draw (12*.5,0.75*.5) node {$\ldots\ldots$};
\filldraw (14*.5,.5) -- (15*.5,1.5*.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.15cm] {$p_{s-1}$} -- (16*.5,2*.5);
\filldraw (14*.5,2*.5) -- (18*.5,0) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.15cm] {$p_s$} -- (19*.5,-0.5*.5);
\end{tikzpicture}
\caption{ : A graph of $\textnormal{D}_n$ type. The straight lines indicate invariant divisors and the solid circles indicate all reduced singularities on these divisors.}\label{fig_Dn}
\end{center}
\end{figure}

By Camacho-Sad formula (Theorem~\ref{thm_CS_formula}), we have, for any $u\in U$, that 
\[-2 = E_{0,1,u}^2 = \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{0,1,u},p_{0,1,u}) \mbox{ and } -2 = E_{0,2,u}^2 = \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{0,2,u},p_{0,2,u}).\]
So $p_{0,1,u}$ and $p_{0,2,u}$ are reduced. 
Thus, 
\begin{align*}
E_{1,u}^2 &= \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{1,u},p_{1,u}) + \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{1,u},p_{0,1,u}) + \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{1,u},p_{0,2,u}) \\
&= \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{1,u},p_{1,u})-\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2}.
\end{align*}
Hence $\lambda_1 := \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{1,u},p_{1,u}) = E_{1,u}^2+1\leq -1$.
\begin{claim}
For all $k=1$, $\ldots$, $s$, $\lambda_k := \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{k,u},p_{k,u})$ are negative rational numbers at most $-1$ and $p_{k,u}$ are reduced non-degenerate singularities. 
\end{claim}
\begin{pf}
We have shown that this holds when $k=1$. 
Assume the claim holds for $k-1$. 
\[-2\geq E_{k,u}^2 = \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{k,u}, p_{k-1,u})+\textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{k,u},p_{k,u}) = \frac{1}{\lambda_{k-1}} + \lambda_{k}. \]
Thus, $\lambda_k\leq -2-\frac{1}{\lambda_{k-1}}\leq -2+1=-1$. 
Hence, $\lambda_k$ is a negative rational number at most $-1$. 
Therefore, $p_{k,u}$ is also a reduced non-degenerate singularity. 
This completes the proof of the claim. 

So the contraction of $E_u$ introduces a dihedral singularity. 
\end{pf}

\item Let $E = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_i$ be a connected component of exceptional divisors such that $E_{t_0} = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_{i,t_0}$ is an \emph{elliptic Gorenstein leaf}. 
Then $E_u = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_{i,u}$ is also an elliptic Gorenstein leaf for all $u\in U$. 
By Lemma~\ref{egl}, all singularities on $E_u$ are reduced and non-degenerate. 
Therefore, the contraction of $E_u$ introduces a cusp singularity. 

\item (Cyclic non-terminal canonical foliation singularities)
Let $E = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_i$ be a connected component of exceptional divisors such that the contraction of $E_{t_0} = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_{i,t_0}$ gives a \emph{cyclic non-terminal} foliation singularity such that $E_{i,t_0}$ are \emph{invariant} for all $i$. 

Then $E_{t_0}$ is a chain of $(-2)$-${\mathcal{G}}_{t_0}$-curves. 
Thus $E_u$ is also a chain of $(-2)$-${\mathcal{G}}_u$-curves for $u\in U$. 
By Lemma~\ref{-2string}, we have the following two cases. 
\begin{enumerate}
\item In the first case, all singularities are reduced. 
So the contraction of $E_u$ introduces a canonical foliation singularity. 
\item In the second case, if all $p_{i,u}$ are reduced (see Figure~\ref{fig_An}), then the contraction of $E_u$ introduces a canonical foliation singularity as well. 

\begin{figure}[h]
\begin{tikzpicture}

\filldraw (2*.5,2*.5) -- (3*.5,1.5*.5) -- (6*.5,0) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.25cm] {$p_2$} -- (7*.5,-0.5*.5);
\filldraw (5*.5,-0.5*.5) -- (6*.5,0) -- (9*.5,1.5*.5) circle (2pt) node[right,xshift=0.25cm] {$p_3$} -- (10*.5,2*.5);

\end{figure}

\begin{claim}
If there is an $i$ such that $p_{i,u}$ is not reduced, then all $p_{j,u}$ are non-degenerate for $j\neq i$. 
\end{claim}
\begin{pf}
Suppose not, then one of $p_{i-1,u}$ and $p_{i+1,u}$ is a saddle-node. 
Without loss of generality, we assume that $p_{i+1,u}$ is a saddle-node and 
\[\textnormal{Z}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{i+1,u},p_{i,u})\leq 0.\]

Let $W_i$ be the irreducible component of the singularities of ${\mathcal{G}}$ containing $p_{i,u}$. 
By Lemma~\ref{eigenvalue}, we have a holomorphic map $\lambda_i : W_i \longrightarrow {\mathbb P}^1$. 
Note that $W_i$ is connected and locally path-connected (in the analytic topology). We have that $W_i$ is path-connected. 
Note that the claim holds true when $\lambda$ is a constant function. 
So we now assume that $\lambda$ is not a constant function. 

There is a sequence $\{w_j\}_{j=1}^\infty$ converging to $p_{i,u}$ such that $\lambda_i(w_j)$ is not a positive rational and converges to $\lambda(p_{i,u})$. 
For any $w_{j}$ close to $p_{i,u}$, there are only two separatrices, one of which is $E_{i+1,\pi(w_j)}$. 
So we may assume $E_{i+1,\pi(w_j)}$ converges to $E_{i+1,u}$. 
Thus $\textnormal{Z}({\mathcal{G}}_u, E_{i+1,u},p_{i,u}) = 1$, which gives a contradiction. 

This completes the proof of the claim. 
\end{pf}

Therefore, the contraction of $E_u$ introduces a mild log canonical foliation singularity. 
\end{enumerate}

\item Let $E = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_i$ be a connected component of exceptional divisors such that the contraction of $E_{t_0} = \bigcup_{i=1}^sE_{i,t_0}$ gives a \emph{cyclic non-canonical foliation singularity}. 
So there is a unique $j\in\{1, \ldots, s\}$ such that $E_{j,t_0}$ is \emph{non-invariant}. 
Since being non-invariant is an open condition, by shrinking $U$ further, we may assume that $E_{u,t_0}$ is non-invariant for all $u\in U$. 

By~(\ref{G-chain}), when $u$ varies, we know that $\bigcup_{i=1}^{j-1}E_{i,u}$ and $\bigcup_{i=j+1}^{s}E_{i,u}$ have the same structures, respectively. 
Therefore, the contraction of $E_u$ introduces a \emph{mild log canonical} foliation singularities. 

\item Fix any $u\in U$, we may contract all $E_u$  where $E$ is any \emph{relative $(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)$-trivial curve}. 
It will end up with a \emph{foliated surface} $(Z,{\mathscr{H}})$ with 
\[K_{{\mathcal{G}}_u}+\Theta_u = \pi^*K_{\mathscr{H}}\] 
where $\pi : Y \longrightarrow Z$ is the contraction morphism. 

\begin{claim}
There is no $K_{{\mathscr{H}}}$-trivial curve $C$ with $C^2<0$. 
\end{claim}
\begin{pf}
Suppose $C$ is a $K_{\mathscr{H}}$-trivial curve with $C^2<0$. 
Then the proper transform $\widetilde{C}$ on $Y$ is a $(K_{{\mathcal{G}}_u}+\Theta_u)$-trivial curve. 
Note that $\widetilde{C}^2\leq C^2<0$. 
Also, by Corollary~\ref{trivial_move}, this $\widetilde{C}$ moves in a family $\mathscr{C}$ with $\mathscr{C}_u = \widetilde{C}$. 
However, $\mathscr{C}_{t_0}^2 = \mathscr{C}_{u}^2 = \widetilde{C}^2<0$ and 
\[(K_{{\mathcal{G}}_{t_0}}+\Theta_{t_0})\cdot\mathscr{C}_{t_0} = (K_{{\mathcal{G}}_u}+\Theta_u)\cdot\mathscr{C}_u = K_{\mathscr{H}}\cdot C = 0.\]
Therefore, \emph{$\mathscr{C}$ is a relative $(K_{\mathcal{G}}+\Theta)$-trivial curve}. 
Hence, $\widetilde{C} = \mathscr{C}_u$ is contracted by $\pi$, which gives a contradiction. 
This completes the proof of the claim. 
\end{pf}

Therefore, $(Z,{\mathscr{H}})$ is a log canonical model and hence $({\mathcal{X}},{\mathcal{F}},\Delta)_u\in{\mathcal{S}}_P$ for any $u\in U$. 
\qed
\end{enumerate}

More explicitly, (a) comes from the generic smoothness. 
For others, let \[S_1 = \bigcup \pi(C)\] 
where the union is taken over all irreducible components $C$ of singularities of ${\mathcal{G}}$ and of exceptional divisors of $g$, which are \emph{not} finite over $U$. 
Let \[S_2 = \bigcup \{t\,\vert\,C_{i,t} = C_{j,t}\}\] 
where the union is taken over all distinct irreducible components $C_i$ and $C_j$ of singularities of ${\mathcal{G}}$. 
Let \[S_3 = \bigcup\pi(C\cap E)\] 
where the union is taken over all irreducible components $C$ of singularity of ${\mathcal{G}}$ and all irreducible components $E$ of exceptional divisors of $g$ such that $C\cap E$ is neither $C$ nor empty. 

Note that $S_1$, $S_2$, and $S_3$ are all proper closed subsets of $U$. 
So by replacing $U$ by $U\setminus (S_1\cup S_2\cup S_3)$, conditions (a)-(d) hold. 
The condition (e) can be achieved since being non-invariant is an open condition.

<!-- claim-7: body_md -->
For all $k=1$, $\ldots$, $s$, $\lambda_k := \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{k,u},p_{k,u})$ are negative rational numbers less than $-1$ and $p_{k,u}$ are reduced non-degenerate singularities.
<!-- end claim-7 -->
<!-- pf-43: body_md -->
We have shown that this holds when $k=1$. 
Assume the claim holds for $k-1$. 
By Camacho-Sad formula (Theorem~\ref{thm_CS_formula}) and Lemma~\ref{lem_ZCS}, we have that 
\[-2\geq E_{k,u}^2 = \textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{k,u}, p_{k-1,u})+\textnormal{CS}({\mathcal{G}}_u,E_{k,u},p_{k,u}) = \frac{1}{\lambda_{k-1}} + \lambda_{k}. \]
Thus, $\lambda_k\leq -2-\frac{1}{\lambda_{k-1}}<-2+1=-1$. 
Hence, $\lambda_k$ is a negative rational number less than $-1$. 
Therefore, $p_{k,u}$ is also a reduced non-degenerate singularity. 
This completes the proof of the claim.
